sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第117卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 117
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 117

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十九】起旃蒙單閼，盡柔兆執徐，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 39] Beginning with Qianmeng Danque, ending with Rouzhao Zhixu, altogether two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 39] Spanning from the year Qianmeng Danque through Rouzhao Zhixu, a period of two years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝壬義熙十一年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, ren year, eleventh year of the Yixi era (
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Yixi era under Emperor An, the ren year (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元四一五年）

translations.literal: yimao, AD 415)
translations.idiomatic: yimao, corresponding to AD 415)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙長，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingchang, the Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, on the day bingchang, the Wei emperor Daowu Tuoba Si returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕收司馬休之次子文寶、兄子文祖，並賜死；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu seized Sima Xiuzhi's second son Wenbao and his elder brother's son Wenzu, and had them both put to death by imperial grant;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu arrested Sima Xiuzhi's second son Wenbao and his nephew Wenzu and had both executed by imperial order;

sentences.zh: 發兵擊之。

translations.literal: he raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: then marched against him at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 詔加裕黃鉞，領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict added the yellow battle-axe to Yu and made him concurrently Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict invested Yu with the yellow battle-axe and appointed him to serve concurrently as Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以吏部尚書謝裕為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Minister of the Civil Service Xie Yu was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Xie Yu, Minister of the Civil Service, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，太尉裕發建康。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Grand Marshal Yu set out from Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Grand Marshal Liu Yu departed from the capital at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍劉道憐監留府事，劉穆之兼右僕射。

translations.literal: He made Central Army General Liu Daolian oversee affairs left at the capital, with Liu Muzhi concurrently serving as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He left Central Army General Liu Daolian in charge of the capital and appointed Liu Muzhi concurrently as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 事無大小，皆決於穆之。

translations.literal: Matters great and small were all decided by Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter, large or small, was decided by Liu Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 又以高陽內史劉鐘領石頭戍事，屯冶亭。

translations.literal: He also had Gaoyang Interior Minister Liu Zhong take charge of the Shitou garrison and encamp at Yeting.
translations.idiomatic: He further assigned Gaoyang Interior Minister Liu Zhong to command the Shitou garrison and camp at Yeting.

sentences.zh: 休之府司馬張裕、南平太守檀范之聞之，皆逃歸建康。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's chief administrator Zhang Yu and Nanping Administrator Tan Fanzhi, on hearing this, all fled back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard the news, Xiuzhi's chief administrator Zhang Yu and Nanping Administrator Tan Fanzhi both fled back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 裕，邵之兄也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu was the elder brother of Zhang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu was the elder brother of Zhang Shao.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史魯宗之自疑不為太尉裕所容，與其子竟陵太守軌起兵應休之。

translations.literal: Yong Province Inspector Lu Zongzhi, doubting that Grand Marshal Yu would tolerate him, rose in arms with his son Jingling Administrator Gui to support Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, Inspector of Yong Province, fearing that Grand Marshal Liu Yu would not spare him, joined his son Gui, Administrator of Jingling, in raising troops to support Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 二月，休之上表罪狀裕，勒兵拒之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Xiuzhi submitted a memorial listing Yu's crimes and mustered troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Xiuzhi memorialized the throne with a bill of indictment against Liu Yu and marshaled his forces to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 裕密書招休之府錄事參軍南陽韓延之，延之復書曰：「承親帥戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不惶駭。

translations.literal: Yu sent a secret letter to recruit Xiuzhi's recording secretary Han Yanzhi of Nanyang; Yanzhi replied in a letter, saying: 'I have learned that you personally lead armed forces and have come far into the western capital region; throughout the whole territory, officials and commoners alike are none but fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent a secret letter trying to win over Xiuzhi's recording secretary Han Yanzhi of Nanyang. Yanzhi wrote back: 'I learn that you are leading troops in person deep into the western heartland; every official and commoner in the region is stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 辱疏，知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: Your honored letter humbles me; I know that because of the former affair of the Prince of Qiao, my sighs have truly increased.
translations.idiomatic: In your gracious letter you mention the affair of the Prince of Qiao; that only deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，款懷待物。

translations.literal: Sima the Pacifier of the West embodies loyalty to the state and treats others with open sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima the Pacifier of the West is loyal to the state in body and open-hearted toward all men.

sentences.zh: 以公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Because you, sir, have the merit of restoring the realm, the house and state have relied upon you; he extended his virtue and entrusted his sincerity, consulting and looking up to you in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Because you had the merit of restoring the dynasty, the house and the realm depended on you; he honored your virtue, entrusted you with his confidence, and sought your counsel in every affair.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao was formerly impeached over a minor matter, yet still memorialized on his own to yield his position;
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qiao was impeached on a trifling charge, he still offered of his own accord to abdicate;

sentences.zh: 況以大過，而錄嘿然邪！

translations.literal: how much more when there was a great fault—yet the records remain silent!
translations.idiomatic: how then could he have kept silent in the face of so grave an offense!

sentences.zh: 前已表奏廢之，所不盡者命耳。

translations.literal: He had already memorialized earlier to depose him; what was not fully accomplished was only a matter of fate.
translations.idiomatic: He had already submitted a memorial calling for the prince's removal; only fate itself could account for what remained undone.

sentences.zh: 推寄相與，正當如此。

translations.literal: The trust placed in one another was just as it should have been.
translations.idiomatic: The mutual trust between them was exactly what such a bond ought to be.

sentences.zh: 而遽興兵甲，所謂『欲加之罪，其無辭乎！』

translations.literal: Yet you suddenly raise arms—what is called, 'If you wish to punish someone, will you not always find a pretext!'
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have suddenly taken up arms—does this not prove the old saying, 'When you wish to punish a man, you will never lack a charge against him!'

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺逛國士！

translations.literal: Liu Yu, beneath your feet—who under heaven does not see this heart of yours, yet you would again deceive and mislead the gentlemen of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, every man under heaven can see what is in your heart; do you imagine you can still deceive the worthies of the realm!

sentences.zh: 來示云『處懷期物，自有由來』，今伐人之君，啖人以利，真可謂『處懷期物，自有由來』者乎！

translations.literal: Your recent message says, 'One who cherishes expectations toward things has reasons that go back long.' Today you attack another man's lord and feed men with profit—can this truly be called 'cherishing expectations toward things with reasons that go back long'!
translations.idiomatic: You write that 'one who harbors designs upon others has his reasons, and they run deep.' Yet now you make war on a sovereign lord and tempt men with gain—is this what you call having reasons that run deep!

sentences.zh: 劉籓死於閶闔之門，諸葛斃於左右之手；

translations.literal: Liu Fan died at the Gate of Heaven, Zhuge [Changmin] was killed by his own attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died at the Gate of Heaven, Zhuge Changmin was struck down by his own attendants;

sentences.zh: 甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵；

translations.literal: with sweet words you deceived the regional lords and struck them with light forces;
translations.idiomatic: with honeyed words you duped the regional commanders, then struck them with a sudden, light strike force;

sentences.zh: 遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以是為得算，良可恥也！

translations.literal: thus causing men of open sincerity to vanish from the court and leaving no self-confident feudal lords beyond the gates; to regard this as a successful calculation is truly shameful!
translations.idiomatic: so that no man of open loyalty remains at court and no lord beyond the frontier dares trust himself—yet you call this sound strategy. It is a disgrace!

sentences.zh: 貴府將佐及朝廷賢德，寄命過日。

translations.literal: The generals and aides of your honored headquarters and the worthy men of the court merely entrust their lives from day to day.
translations.idiomatic: The officers of your own staff and the worthy men at court merely live from day to day at your pleasure.

sentences.zh: 吾誠鄙劣，嘗聞道於君子，以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎！

translations.literal: I am indeed base and inferior, yet I have once heard the Way from gentlemen; with the supreme virtue of the Pacifier of the West, how could there fail to be ministers who would receive his command unto death!
translations.idiomatic: I am a mean and worthless man, yet I have learned from gentlemen what honor demands. With the Pacifier of the West's supreme virtue, can he lack ministers who would die at his command!

sentences.zh: 必未能自投虎口，比跡郗僧施之徒明矣。

translations.literal: I certainly could not throw myself into the tiger's maw of my own accord; to compare my footsteps with men like Xi Sengshi is abundantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: I shall certainly not throw myself into the tiger's maw of my own will. That I am no Xi Sengshi should be plain enough.

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪游於地下，不復多言。」

translations.literal: If heaven should long prolong chaos and the nine currents grow turbid, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong—no more words.'
translations.idiomatic: Should heaven prolong this age of disorder until all the world runs foul, I shall keep company with Zang Hong in the world below. I have nothing more to say.'

sentences.zh: 裕視書歎息，以示將佐曰：「事人當如此矣！」

translations.literal: Yu read the letter and sighed, showing it to his generals and aides, saying: 'To serve a man ought to be like this!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu read the letter and sighed. He showed it to his officers and said, 'This is how one ought to serve one's lord!'

sentences.zh: 延之以裕父名翹，字顯宗。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, because Yu's father's name was Qiao and his style was Xianzong,
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, knowing that Liu Yu's father's name was Qiao and his style Xianzong,

sentences.zh: 乃更其字曰顯宗，名其子曰翹，以示不臣劉氏。

translations.literal: thereupon changed his own style to Xianzong and named his son Qiao, to show that he would not serve the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: changed his own style to Xianzong and named his son Qiao, thereby declaring that he would not submit to the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 琅邪太守劉朗帥二千餘家降魏。

translations.literal: Langye Administrator Liu Lang led more than two thousand households in surrendering to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lang, Administrator of Langye, led more than two thousand households in surrendering to Wei.

sentences.zh: 庚子，河西胡劉雲等帥數萬戶降魏。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Hexi Hu Liu Yun and others led tens of thousands of households in surrendering to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Liu Yun of the Hexi Hu and others led tens of thousands of households in submitting to Wei.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕吏參軍檀道濟、朱超石將步騎出襄陽。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu's staff adviser Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi led infantry and cavalry out from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi, staff advisers to Grand Marshal Liu Yu, led infantry and cavalry out of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 超石，齡石之弟也。

translations.literal: Chao-shi was the younger brother of Ling-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chao-shi was the younger brother of Zhu Ling-shi.

sentences.zh: 江夏太守劉虔之將兵屯三連，立橋聚糧以待，道濟等積日不至。

translations.literal: Jiangxia Administrator Liu Qianzhi led troops to encamp at Sanlian, built bridges, and gathered grain to await them, but Daoji and the others did not arrive for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qianzhi, Administrator of Jiangxia, marched to Sanlian, built bridges, and stockpiled grain to await Tan Daoji's force, but Daoji and his men failed to arrive for many days.

sentences.zh: 魯軌襲擊虔之，殺之。

translations.literal: Lu Gui launched a surprise attack on Qianzhi and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gui attacked Qianzhi by surprise and killed him.

sentences.zh: 裕使其婿振威將軍東海徐逵之統參軍蒯恩、王允之、沈淵子為前鋒，出江夏口。

translations.literal: Yu had his son-in-law Zhenwei General Xu Kuizhi of Donghai command the staff officers Kuai En, Wang Yunzhi, and Shen Yuanzi as the vanguard, advancing from Jiangxiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent his son-in-law Xu Kuizhi of Donghai, General Who Quells Might, to lead the staff officers Kuai En, Wang Yunzhi, and Shen Yuanzi as the vanguard out of Jiangxiakou.

sentences.zh: 逵之等與魯軌戰於破塚，兵敗，逵之、允之、淵子皆死，獨蒯恩勒兵不動。

translations.literal: Kuizhi and the others fought Lu Gui at Pozhong and were defeated; Kuizhi, Yunzhi, and Yuanzi all died, while Kuai En alone held his troops motionless.
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhi and his men fought Lu Gui at Pozhong and were routed. Kuizhi, Yunzhi, and Yuanzi were all killed; only Kuai En held his troops firm and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 軌乘勝力攻之，不能克，乃退。

translations.literal: Gui pressed his advantage and attacked him with all his strength but could not overcome him, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pressed the attack at full strength but could not break Kuai En's line and finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 淵子，林子之兄也。

translations.literal: Yuanzi was the elder brother of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuanzi was the elder brother of Shen Linzi.

sentences.zh: 裕軍於馬頭，聞逵之死，怒甚。

translations.literal: Yu encamped at Matou; on hearing of Kuizhi's death, he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu encamped at Matou. When he heard of Kuizhi's death, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬午，帥諸將濟江。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renwu, he led the generals across the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renwu, he led his generals across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 魯軌、司馬文思將休之兵四萬，臨峭岸置陳，軍士無能登者。

translations.literal: Lu Gui and Sima Wensi commanded Xiuzhi's forty thousand troops, drew up battle lines along a steep bank, and none of the soldiers could climb up.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gui and Sima Wensi commanded Xiuzhi's army of forty thousand men, arrayed along a sheer bank where none of Liu Yu's soldiers could gain a foothold.

sentences.zh: 裕自被甲欲登，諸將諫，不從，怒愈甚。

translations.literal: Yu himself donned armor and wished to climb up; the generals remonstrated, but he would not listen, and his anger grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu himself buckled on armor and prepared to climb the bank. His generals pleaded with him, but he would not listen, and his rage only mounted.

sentences.zh: 太尉主簿謝晦前抱持裕，裕抽劍指晦曰：「我斬卿！」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal chief clerk Xie Hui went forward and seized Yu in his arms; Yu drew his sword and pointed it at Hui, saying: 'I will cut you down!'
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, rushed forward and seized Liu Yu in his arms. Liu Yu drew his sword and pointed it at Hui, crying, 'I will kill you!'

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「天下可無晦，不可無公！」

translations.literal: Hui said: 'The realm can do without Hui, but it cannot do without you, my lord!'
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, 'The realm can spare Hui, but it cannot spare you, my lord!'

sentences.zh: 建武將軍胡籓領遊兵在江津，裕呼籓使登，籓有疑色。

translations.literal: Jianwu General Hu Fan commanded the mobile troops at Jiangjin; Yu called Fan to climb up, and Fan showed a look of hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu General Hu Fan commanded the mobile troops at Jiangjin. Liu Yu ordered Fan to climb the bank, but Fan hesitated.

sentences.zh: 裕命左右錄來，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Yu ordered his attendants to seize and bring him forward, intending to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu ordered his attendants to seize Fan and bring him forward for execution.

sentences.zh: 籓顧曰：「正欲擊賊，不得奉教！」

translations.literal: Fan looked back and said: 'I was just about to strike the rebels—I could not obey your command!'
translations.idiomatic: Fan turned and cried, 'I was about to strike the enemy—I could not wait for your order!'

sentences.zh: 乃以刀頭穿岸，劣容足指，騰之而上，隨之者稍多。

translations.literal: Thereupon he used the tip of his blade to pierce the bank, barely enough for the toes of his feet, and vaulted upward; those who followed him gradually grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He wedged the point of his blade into the bank, found footing for no more than his toes, and vaulted upward. Others followed, and soon a growing number were climbing after him.

sentences.zh: 既登岸，直前力戰。

translations.literal: Once they had climbed ashore, they pressed straight forward and fought with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Once ashore, they pressed straight ahead and fought with all their might.

sentences.zh: 休之兵不能當，稍引卻。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's troops could not withstand them and gradually drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's troops could not hold them and slowly gave ground.

sentences.zh: 裕兵因而乘之，休之兵大潰，遂克江陵。

translations.literal: Yu's troops thereupon pressed the advantage; Xiuzhi's army was utterly routed, and they then captured Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's men pressed the advantage, Xiuzhi's army broke in complete rout, and they took Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 休之、宗之俱北走，軌留石城。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and Zongzhi both fled north together; Gui remained at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi and Zongzhi both fled north together, while Gui held Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 裕命閬中侯下邳趙倫之、太尉參軍沈林子攻之；

translations.literal: Yu ordered Langzhong Marquis Zhao Lunzhi of Xiapi and Grand Marshal staff officer Shen Linzi to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu ordered Zhao Lunzhi of Xiapi, Marquis of Langzhong, and his staff officer Shen Linzi to attack Shicheng;

sentences.zh: 遣武陵內史王鎮惡以舟師追休之等。

translations.literal: he dispatched Wuling Interior Minister Wang Zhen'e with a naval force to pursue Xiuzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Wang Zhen'e, Interior Minister of Wuling, with a fleet in pursuit of Xiuzhi and his party.

sentences.zh: 有群盜數百夜襲冶亭，京師震駭；

translations.literal: A band of several hundred robbers attacked Yeting by night, and the capital was shaken with alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred bandits raided Yeting by night, throwing the capital into alarm;

sentences.zh: 劉鐘討平之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhong suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong marched out and put them down.

sentences.zh: 秦廣平公弼譖姚宣於秦王興，宣司馬權丕至長安，興責以不能輔導，將誅之；

translations.literal: Qin Prince of Guangping Bi slandered Yao Xuan to Qin King Xing; Xuan's chief administrator Quan Pi arrived at Chang'an, and Xing blamed him for failing to guide and instruct, intending to put him to death;
translations.idiomatic: In Qin, the Prince of Guangping, Yao Bi, slandered Yao Xuan to King Yao Xing. When Xuan's chief administrator Quan Pi reached Chang'an, Xing blamed him for failing to guide his lord properly and was about to execute him;

sentences.zh: 丕懼，誣宣罪惡以求自免。

translations.literal: Pi was afraid and falsely accused Xuan of crimes in order to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, in fear for his life, falsely accused Xuan of crimes in the hope of saving himself.

sentences.zh: 興怒，遣使就杏城收宣下獄，命弼將三萬人鎮秦州。

translations.literal: Xing was enraged, sent envoys to Xingcheng to seize Xuan and cast him into prison, and ordered Bi to lead thirty thousand men to garrison Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xing flew into a rage, sent envoys to Xingcheng to arrest Xuan and throw him into prison, and ordered Bi to lead thirty thousand men to garrison Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 尹昭曰：「廣平公與皇太子不平，今握強兵於外，陛下一旦不諱，社稷必危。

translations.literal: Yin Zhao said: 'The Prince of Guangping is at odds with the Crown Prince; now he holds a strong army abroad. If Your Majesty should one day pass away, the altars of state will surely be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhao said, 'The Prince of Guangping is at odds with the Crown Prince, yet now he commands a large army in the field. Should Your Majesty meet with misfortune, the realm itself will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 『小不忍，亂大謀』，陛下之謂也。」

translations.literal: 'He who will not bear a little ends by ruining a great plan'—this is what applies to Your Majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: 'He who will not bear a little ends by ruining a great plan'—that proverb was written for Your Majesty.'

sentences.zh: 興不從。

translations.literal: Xing did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃攻秦杏城，拔之，執守將姚逵，坑士卒二萬人。

translations.literal: Xia King Bobo attacked Qin's Xingcheng, took it, seized the defending general Yao Kui, and buried alive twenty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo, king of Xia, attacked Xingcheng in Qin, captured it, seized the garrison commander Yao Kui, and buried alive twenty thousand of his troops.

sentences.zh: 秦王興如北地，遣廣平公弼及輔國將軍斂曼嵬向新平，興還長安。

translations.literal: Qin King Xing went to Beidi, dispatched the Prince of Guangping Bi and Supporting-the-State General Qiumanwei toward Xinping, and Xing returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing of Qin went to Beidi and dispatched the Prince of Guangping, Yao Bi, and Supporting-the-State General Qiumanwei toward Xinping, then returned to Chang'an himself.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜攻西秦廣武郡，拔之。

translations.literal: Hexi King Mengxun attacked Western Qin's Guangwu Commandery and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun, king of Hexi, attacked Guangwu Commandery in Western Qin and captured it.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐遣將軍乞伏魋尼寅邀蒙遜於浩宜，蒙遜擊斬之；

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan dispatched General Qifu Kuiniyin to intercept Mengxun at Haoyi; Mengxun attacked and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Chipan, king of Western Qin, sent General Qifu Kuiniyin to intercept Mengxun at Haoyi; Mengxun attacked and killed him;

sentences.zh: 又遣將軍折斐等帥騎一萬據勒姐嶺，蒙孫擊禽之。

translations.literal: he also dispatched Generals Zhe Fei and others to lead ten thousand horsemen to hold Lejie Ridge; Mengxun attacked and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan also sent Generals Zhe Fei and others with ten thousand horsemen to hold Lejie Ridge; Mengxun attacked and captured them.

sentences.zh: 河西饑胡相聚於上黨，推胡人白惡栗斯為單于，改元建平，以司馬順宰為謀主，寇魏河內。

translations.literal: Starving Hu of Hexi gathered at Shangdang, made the Hu man Bai Elisi their chanyu, changed the era name to Jianping, took Sima Shunzai as their chief strategist, and raided Wei's Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Starving Hu tribesmen of Hexi gathered at Shangdang, proclaimed the Hu leader Bai Elisi as chanyu, adopted the era name Jianping, made Sima Shunzai their chief strategist, and raided Henei in Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏主嗣命公孫表等五將討之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Wei ruler Si ordered Gongsun Biao and four other generals to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, the Wei emperor Si ordered Gongsun Biao and four other generals to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史劉敬宣參軍司馬道賜，宗室之疏屬也。

translations.literal: Qing and Ji Provinces Inspector Liu Jingxuan's staff officer Sima Daoci was a distant member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daoci, a staff officer to Liu Jingxuan, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was a distant kinsman of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 聞太尉裕攻司馬休之，道賜與同府辟閭道秀、左右小將王猛子謀殺敬宣，據廣固以應休之。

translations.literal: On hearing that Grand Marshal Yu was attacking Sima Xiuzhi, Daoci joined with his colleague Pilu Daoxiu and the junior officer Wang Mengzi in a plot to kill Jingxuan, seize Guanggu, and respond to Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Grand Marshal Liu Yu was attacking Sima Xiuzhi, Daoci conspired with his colleague Pilu Daoxiu and the junior officer Wang Mengzi to murder Jingxuan, seize Guanggu, and join Xiuzhi's cause.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，敬宣召道秀，屏人語，左右悉出戶。

translations.literal: On yimao, Jingxuan summoned Daoxiu, dismissed the attendants to speak in private, and all those at his side went out through the door.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Jingxuan summoned Daoxiu for a private talk and sent everyone else out of the room.

sentences.zh: 猛子逡巡在後，取敬宣備身刀殺敬宣。

translations.literal: Mengzi lingered behind and, taking Jingxuan's bodyguard sword, killed Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzi lingered behind, drew Jingxuan's bodyguard sword, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 文武佐吏即時討道賜等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: The civil and military aides immediately attacked Daoci and the others, and all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan's civil and military officers at once moved against Daoci and his accomplices and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏主嗣北巡。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Wei ruler Si made a northern tour of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the Wei emperor Si set out on a tour of inspection in the north.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐子元基自長安逃歸，熾磐以為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan's son Yuanji fled back from Chang'an; Chipan made him Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji, son of Chipan, king of Western Qin, escaped from Chang'an and returned home; Chipan appointed him Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥，魏主嗣如大寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the Wei ruler Si went to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the Wei emperor Si went to Daning.

sentences.zh: 趙倫之、沈林子破魯軌於石城，司馬休之、魯宗之救之不及，遂與軌奔襄陽，宗之參軍李應之閉門不納。

translations.literal: Zhao Lunzhi and Shen Linzi defeated Lu Gui at Shicheng; Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi could not rescue him in time and thereupon fled with Gui toward Xiangyang, but Zongzhi's staff officer Li Yingzhi closed the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lunzhi and Shen Linzi defeated Lu Gui at Shicheng. Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi arrived too late to save him and fled with Gui toward Xiangyang, but Li Yingzhi, a staff officer under Zongzhi, shut the gates and refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 甲午，休之、宗之、軌及譙王文思、新蔡王道賜、梁州刺史馬敬、南陽太守魯范俱奔秦。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Xiuzhi, Zongzhi, Gui, and the Prince of Qiao Wensi, the Prince of Xincai Daoci, Liang Province Inspector Ma Jing, and Nanyang Administrator Lu Fan all fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Xiuzhi, Zongzhi, Gui, Wensi Prince of Qiao, Daoci Prince of Xincai, Ma Jing Inspector of Liang Province, and Lu Fan Administrator of Nanyang all fled to Qin.

sentences.zh: 宗之素得士民心，爭為之衛送出境。

translations.literal: Zongzhi had long won the hearts of scholars and commoners, who vied with one another to escort and guard him out of the border.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi had long enjoyed the loyalty of the gentry and the common people, who vied with one another to guard and escort him out of Jin territory.

sentences.zh: 王鎮晉等追之，盡境而還。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenjin and the others pursued them and returned only after reaching the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e and his men pursued them to the frontier and then turned back.

sentences.zh: 初，休之等求救於秦、魏，秦征虜將軍姚成王及司馬國璠引兵至南陽，魏長孫嵩至河東，聞休之等敗，皆引還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiuzhi and the others had sought aid from Qin and Wei; Qin's General Who Subdues the Barbarians Yao Chengwang and Sima Guofan led troops to Nanyang, and Wei's Changsun Song reached Hedong; on hearing that Xiuzhi and the others had been defeated, they all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiuzhi and his party had appealed for help to Qin and Wei. Yao Chengwang, Qin's General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Sima Guofan marched to Nanyang, while Changsun Song of Wei reached Hedong; when they heard that Xiuzhi had been defeated, both forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 休之至長安，秦王興以為揚州刺史，使侵擾襄陽。

translations.literal: When Xiuzhi reached Chang'an, Qin King Xing made him Governor of Yang Province and had him harass and raid Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuzhi reached Chang'an, King Yao Xing appointed him Governor of Yang Province and set him to raiding Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 待御史唐盛言於興曰：「據符讖之文，司馬氏當復得河、洛。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Tang Sheng said to Xing: 'According to the texts of prognostications, the Sima house ought to recover the Yellow and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Tang Sheng said to Xing, 'According to the prognostic texts, the house of Sima is destined to recover the lands between the Yellow and Luo rivers.

sentences.zh: 今使休之擅兵於外，猶縱魚於淵也；

translations.literal: Now to let Xiuzhi wield troops on his own abroad is like releasing a fish into the deep;
translations.idiomatic: To let Xiuzhi command troops on his own in the field is like releasing a fish back into the deep;

sentences.zh: 不如以高爵厚禮，留之京師。」

translations.literal: it would be better to honor him with high rank and generous treatment and keep him in the capital.'
translations.idiomatic: it would be wiser to honor him with high rank and rich rewards and keep him at court.'

sentences.zh: 興曰：「昔文王卒羑裡，高祖不斃鴻門；

translations.literal: Xing said: 'In olden days King Wen died at Youli, yet the High Ancestor was not killed at Hong Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Xing replied, 'King Wen of Zhou died a prisoner at Youli, yet the High Ancestor of Han was not killed at Hong Gate;

sentences.zh: 苟天命所在，誰能違之！

translations.literal: if the Mandate of Heaven is where it lies, who can go against it!
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven's mandate rests where it will, who can defy it!

sentences.zh: 脫如符讖之言，留之適足為害。」

translations.literal: If the prognostic texts should prove true, keeping him would only add to the harm.'
translations.idiomatic: If the prognostications are true, keeping him here would only make matters worse.'

sentences.zh: 遂遣之。

translations.literal: He then sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 詔加太尉裕太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: An edict elevated Grand Marshal Yu to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province, granted him the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the palace hall, of not hastening when entering court, and of not having his name spoken during ceremonial salutations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Grand Marshal Liu Yu to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province, with the privileges of wearing sword and shoes in the palace hall, entering court without hurrying, and being addressed without his name during ceremonial salutations.

sentences.zh: 以兗、青二州刺史劉道憐為都督荊、湘、益、秦、寧、、雍七州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Daolian, Governor of Yan and Qing provinces, was made Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the seven provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Qin, Ning, [—], and Yong, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daolian, who held Yan and Qing provinces, was appointed Commander-in-Chief over the seven provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Qin, Ning, [—], and Yong, made General of Agile Cavalry, and named Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 道憐貪鄙，無才能，裕以中軍長史晉陵太守謝方明為驃騎長史、南郡相，道憐府中眾事皆咨決於方明。

translations.literal: Daolian was greedy and base, without ability; Yu made Central Army Chief Clerk and Jinling Administrator Xie Fangming Chief Clerk to the General of Agile Cavalry and Chancellor of Nan Commandery, and all affairs in Daolian's headquarters were consulted and decided by Fangming.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian was greedy and untalented. Yu appointed Xie Fangming, chief clerk of the central army and administrator of Jinling, as chief clerk to the General of Agile Cavalry and chancellor of Nan Commandery; every matter in Daolian's headquarters was referred to Fangming for decision.

sentences.zh: 方明，沖之子也。

translations.literal: Fangming was the son of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming was the son of Xie Chong.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史朱齡石遣使詣河西王蒙遜，諭以朝廷威德。

translations.literal: Yi Province Inspector Zhu Lingshi sent an envoy to the King of Hexi, Mengsun, to instruct him in the court's majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, Governor of Yi Province, sent an envoy to Juqu Mengsun, King of Hexi, to impress upon him the authority and benevolence of the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣舍人黃迅詣齡石，且上表言：「伏聞車騎將軍裕欲清中原，願為右翼，驅除戎虜。」

translations.literal: Mengsun sent Attendant Huang Xun to Lingshi and also submitted a memorial saying: 'I have heard that General of Chariots and Cavalry Yu wishes to cleanse the Central Plains; I wish to serve as his right wing and drive off the barbarian invaders.'
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun sent his attendant Huang Xun to Lingshi and submitted a memorial stating, 'I have learned that General of Chariots and Cavalry Liu Yu intends to recover the Central Plains; I wish to serve on his right flank and help expel the barbarian foe.'

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃遣御史中丞烏洛孤與蒙遜結盟，蒙遜遣其弟湟河太守漢平蒞盟於夏。

translations.literal: Xia King Bobo sent Supervising Censor Wuluogu to form an alliance with Mengsun; Mengsun sent his younger brother Hanping, Administrator of Huanghe, to attend the alliance at Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo, King of Xia, sent Supervising Censor Wuluogu to ally with Mengsun; Mengsun in turn sent his younger brother Hanping, governor of Huanghe, to Xia to seal the pact.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐帥眾三萬襲湟河，沮渠漢平拒之，遣司馬隗仁夜出擊熾磐，破之。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan led thirty thousand men to raid Huanghe; Juqu Hanping resisted him and sent Major Wei Ren out by night to strike Chipan and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Western Qin, led thirty thousand troops in a raid on Huanghe. Juqu Hanping held him off and sent his major Wei Ren on a night attack that routed Chipan's force.

sentences.zh: 熾磐將引去，漢平長史焦昶、將軍段景潛召熾磐，熾磐復攻之，昶、景因說漢平出降。

translations.literal: Chipan was about to withdraw when Hanping's chief clerk Jiao Chang and General Duan Jing secretly summoned Chipan back; Chipan attacked again, and Chang and Jing thereupon persuaded Hanping to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan was preparing to withdraw when Hanping's chief clerk Jiao Chang and General Duan Jing secretly recalled him. Chipan renewed the assault, and Chang and Jing then persuaded Hanping to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁勒壯士百餘據南門樓，三日不下，力屈，為熾磐所禽。

translations.literal: Ren rallied more than a hundred stalwart men to hold the south gate tower; for three days they did not come down, but when their strength was exhausted he was captured by Chipan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ren gathered more than a hundred stalwart fighters and held the south gate tower for three days without yielding; when his strength gave out, Chipan captured him.

sentences.zh: 熾磐欲斬之，散騎常侍武威段暉諫曰：「仁臨難不畏死，忠臣也，宜宥之以厲事君。」

translations.literal: Chipan wished to execute him; Attendant-in-Ordinary Duan Hui of Wuwei remonstrated, saying: 'Ren, facing danger, did not fear death—he is a loyal minister; he should be pardoned to encourage service to one's lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Chipan wanted to execute him, but Attendant-in-Ordinary Duan Hui of Wuwei remonstrated, 'Wei Ren did not flinch from death in the face of danger—he is a loyal minister. Pardon him, and others will be inspired to serve their lords faithfully.'

sentences.zh: 乃囚之。

translations.literal: He then imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan then had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 熾磐以左衛將軍匹達為湟河太守，擊乙弗窟乾，降其三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Chipan made Left Guard General Pida Administrator of Huanghe, attacked Yifu Kugan, and received the surrender of more than three thousand households before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan appointed Left Guard General Pida governor of Huanghe, attacked Yifu Kugan, accepted the surrender of more than three thousand households, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射出連虔為都督嶺北諸軍事、涼州刺史；

translations.literal: He made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chilian Qian Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs north of the mountain passes and Governor of Liang Province;
translations.idiomatic: He made Right Vice Director Chilian Qian Commander-in-Chief of the forces north of the passes and Governor of Liang Province;

sentences.zh: 以涼州刺史謙屯為鎮軍大將軍、河州牧。

translations.literal: he made Liang Province Inspector Qiantun General Who Stabilizes the Army and Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: and he made Qiantun, governor of Liang Province, General Who Stabilizes the Army and Governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 隗仁在西秦五年，段暉又為之請，熾磐免之，使還姑臧。

translations.literal: Wei Ren remained in Western Qin for five years; Duan Hui again pleaded on his behalf, and Chipan released him and sent him back to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ren spent five years in Western Qin captivity. Duan Hui pleaded for him again, and Chipan set him free and sent him back to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏主嗣行如濡源，遂至上谷、涿鹿、廣寧。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Wei ruler Si traveled to Ruyuan and then on to Shanggu, Zhuolu, and Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Emperor Si of Wei traveled to Ruyuan and continued on to Shanggu, Zhuolu, and Guangning.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，還平城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiwei, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐以秦州刺史曇達為尚書令，光祿勳王松壽為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan made Qin Province Inspector Tanda Minister of the Masters of Writing and Household Minister Wang Songsou Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Western Qin, appointed Tanda, governor of Qin Province, Minister of the Masters of Writing, and made Household Minister Wang Songsou governor of Qin Province in his place.

sentences.zh: 辛亥晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of xinhai, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the xinhai cycle, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，太尉裕還建康，固辭太傅、州牧，其餘受命。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiazi, Grand Marshal Yu returned to Jiankang, firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor and provincial governor, and accepted the rest of the appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiazi, Grand Marshal Liu Yu returned to Jiankang. He firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor and provincial governor but accepted the remaining honors.

sentences.zh: 以豫章公世子義符為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir of the Duke of Yuzhang, Yifu, was made Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yifu, heir of the Duke of Yuzhang, was appointed Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 丁未，謝裕卒；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Xie Yu died;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Xie Yu died;

sentences.zh: 以劉穆之為左僕射。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was appointed Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 九月，己亥，大赦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jihai, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 魏比歲霜旱，雲、代之民多饑死。

translations.literal: In Wei, frost and drought continued year after year, and many people in Yun and Dai died of famine.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, successive years of frost and drought left many people in Yun and Dai dead of starvation.

sentences.zh: 太史令王亮、蘇坦言於魏主嗣曰：「按讖書，魏當都鄴，可得豐樂。」

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Wang Liang and Suyan said to the Wei ruler Si: 'According to prognostic books, Wei ought to make its capital at Ye, where abundance and joy may be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Wang Liang and Suyan said to Emperor Si of Wei, 'According to the prognostic texts, Wei should move its capital to Ye, where the realm would enjoy abundance and prosperity.'

sentences.zh: 嗣以問群臣，博士祭酒崔浩、特進京兆周澹曰：「遷都於鄴，可以救今年之饑，非久長之計也。

translations.literal: Si questioned the ministers about it; Libationer of the Academy Cui Hao and Special Advancement Zhou Dan of Jingzhao said: 'Moving the capital to Ye could relieve this year's famine, but it is not a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Si put the question to his ministers. Libationer Cui Hao and Special Advancement Zhou Dan of Jingzhao replied, 'Moving the capital to Ye might ease this year's famine, but it is no lasting solution.

sentences.zh: 山東之人，以國家居廣漠之地，謂其民畜無涯，號曰『牛毛之眾』。

translations.literal: The people of Shandong, because the state dwelt in vast desert lands, believed its people and livestock were boundless and called them 'a multitude like cattle hair.'
translations.idiomatic: The people east of the mountains, seeing the state established in vast steppe lands, believed its population and herds were inexhaustible and called them 'a multitude like cattle hair.'

sentences.zh: 今留兵守舊都，分家南徙，不能滿諸州之地，參居郡縣，情見事露，恐四方皆有輕侮之心；

translations.literal: Now if troops are left to guard the old capital while families are divided and moved south, they cannot fill the lands of the various provinces or be distributed among the commanderies and counties; once the truth is exposed, I fear all quarters will harbor contempt;
translations.idiomatic: If we leave troops to guard the old capital while families are split up and moved south, they cannot populate the provinces or be scattered through the commanderies and counties. Once the truth is exposed, every quarter of the realm may look on us with contempt;

sentences.zh: 且百姓不便水土，疾疫死傷者必多。

translations.literal: moreover, the common people will not adapt to the water and soil, and those who die of pestilence and injury will surely be many.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the people will not adapt to the new climate and soil, and deaths from disease will be heavy.

sentences.zh: 又，舊都守兵既少，屈丐、柔然將有窺窬之心，舉國而來，雲中、平城必危，朝廷隔恆、代千里之險，難以赴救，此則聲實俱損也。

translations.literal: Again, with so few troops guarding the old capital, Juqu Mengsun and Rouran will harbor designs of encroachment; if they come with their whole states, Yunzhong and Pingcheng will surely be endangered, and with the court separated from Heng and Dai by a thousand li of perilous terrain, rescue will be hard to send—thus both reputation and substance will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, with so few troops left to guard the old capital, Juqu Mengsun and Rouran will be tempted to encroach. If they march in full force, Yunzhong and Pingcheng will be in peril, and with the court cut off from Heng and Dai by a thousand li of difficult terrain, relief will be hard to send. Both our prestige and our substance would suffer.

sentences.zh: 今居北方，假令山東有變，我輕騎南下，布濩林薄之間，孰能知其多少！

translations.literal: Now, dwelling in the north, suppose there is trouble in Shandong—we could send light cavalry south and spread them through woods and thickets; who could know how many we are!
translations.idiomatic: As long as we remain in the north, if trouble arises in Shandong we can send light cavalry south and spread them through forest and thicket—who could tell how many we truly are!

sentences.zh: 百姓望塵懾服，此國家所以威制諸夏也。

translations.literal: The common people, seeing the dust of our approach, are awed into submission—this is how the state overawes all Xia by its might.
translations.idiomatic: When the people see our dust on the horizon, they submit in awe—this is how the state keeps the Chinese realms in check.

sentences.zh: 來春草生，湩酪將出，兼以菜果，得以秋熟，則事濟矣。」

translations.literal: When grass grows next spring and mare's milk and cheese come forth, together with vegetables and fruit, and the autumn harvest ripens, the matter will be settled.'
translations.idiomatic: When grass returns in spring, mare's milk and cheese will be available again, and with vegetables, fruit, and the autumn harvest, the crisis will pass.'

sentences.zh: 嗣曰：「今倉廩空竭，既無以待來秋，若來秋又饑，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Si said: 'Now the granaries are empty and exhausted; there is nothing with which to await next autumn—if next autumn brings famine again, what then shall we do?'
translations.idiomatic: Si asked, 'Our granaries are empty. We have nothing to carry us to next autumn. If famine comes again then, what are we to do?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「宜簡饑貧之戶，使就谷山東；

translations.literal: They replied: 'The hungry and impoverished households should be selected and sent to find grain in Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: They answered, 'Select the poorest and hungriest households and send them to find grain in Shandong;

sentences.zh: 若來秋復饑，當更圖之，但方今不可遷都耳。」

translations.literal: if famine returns next autumn, another plan may be devised, but for the present the capital must not be moved.'
translations.idiomatic: if famine returns next autumn, we can devise another plan—but for now the capital must not be moved.'

sentences.zh: 嗣悅，曰：「唯二人與朕意同。」

translations.literal: Si was pleased and said: 'Only these two men share my mind.'
translations.idiomatic: Si was pleased and said, 'Only these two share my thinking.'

sentences.zh: 乃簡國人尤貧者詣山東三州就食，遣左部尚書代人周幾帥眾鎮魯口以安集之。

translations.literal: He then selected the poorest of the state's people and sent them to the three Shandong provinces to obtain food, and dispatched Left Department Minister Zhou Ji of the Dai people to lead troops and garrison Lukou to settle and gather them.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected the poorest of his subjects and sent them to the three Shandong provinces for relief, dispatching Left Department Minister Zhou Ji to garrison Lukou with troops and settle them there.

sentences.zh: 嗣躬耕藉田，且命有司勸課農桑。

translations.literal: Si personally plowed the sacred field and also ordered the officials to encourage and inspect agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Si personally plowed the sacred field and ordered the officials to promote and supervise farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 明年，大熟，民遂富安。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great harvest, and the people became prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: The following year brought a bumper harvest, and the people grew prosperous and secure.

sentences.zh: 夏赫連建將兵擊秦，執平涼太守姚周都。

translations.literal: Xia's Helian Jian led troops to attack Qin and captured Pingliang Administrator Yao Zhoudu.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Jian of Xia led troops against Qin and captured Yao Zhoudu, governor of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 遂入新平。

translations.literal: He then entered Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Xinping.

sentences.zh: 廣平公弼與戰於龍尾堡，禽之。

translations.literal: Duke of Guangping Bi fought him at Longwei Fort and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Guangping, Yao Bi, fought him at Longwei Fort and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 秦王興藥動。

translations.literal: Qin King Xing's illness stirred.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing's illness grew worse.

sentences.zh: 廣平公弼稱疾不朝，聚兵於第。

translations.literal: Duke of Guangping Bi claimed illness and did not attend court, gathering troops at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Guangping, Yao Bi, feigned illness and stayed away from court while gathering troops at his residence.

sentences.zh: 興聞之，怒，收弼黨唐盛、孫玄等殺之。

translations.literal: When Xing heard of it he was angry, seized Bi's partisans Tang Sheng, Sun Xuan, and others, and put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing learned of this he was enraged. He arrested Bi's associates Tang Sheng, Sun Xuan, and others and executed them.

sentences.zh: 太子泓請曰：「臣不肖，不能緝諧兄弟，使至於此，皆臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hong pleaded: 'Your servant is unworthy and could not harmonize his brothers, bringing matters to this pass—all of it is your servant's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yao Hong pleaded, 'I am unworthy. I failed to keep harmony among my brothers and brought matters to this pass—the fault is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 若臣死而國家安，願賜臣死；

translations.literal: If your servant's death would bring peace to the state, I beg to be granted death;
translations.idiomatic: If my death would bring the state peace, I beg you to grant it;

sentences.zh: 若陛下不忍殺臣，乞退就籓。」

translations.literal: if Your Majesty cannot bear to kill your servant, I beg to withdraw and take up a fief.'
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty cannot bring yourself to execute me, I beg leave to withdraw to my fief.'

sentences.zh: 興惻然憫之，召姚贊、梁喜、尹昭、斂曼嵬與之謀，囚弼，將殺之，窮治黨與。

translations.literal: Xing was moved with pity for him; he summoned Yao Zan, Liang Xi, Yin Zhao, and Qian Manwei to consult with him, imprisoned Bi, was about to execute him, and pursued the investigation of his partisans to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was moved to pity. He summoned Yao Zan, Liang Xi, Yin Zhao, and Qian Manwei to deliberate, imprisoned Bi, and prepared to execute him while pursuing his associates to the end.

sentences.zh: 泓流涕固請，乃並其黨赦之。

translations.literal: Hong, weeping, firmly pleaded, and then he and his partisans were pardoned together.
translations.idiomatic: Hong wept and pleaded insistently, and in the end Bi and his associates were pardoned together.

sentences.zh: 泓待弼如初，無忿恨之色。

translations.literal: Hong treated Bi as at first, with no sign of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong treated Bi exactly as before, with no trace of resentment.

sentences.zh: 魏太史奏：「熒惑在匏瓜中，忽亡不知所在，於法當入危亡之國，先為童謠妖言，然後行其禍罰。」

translations.literal: The Wei Grand Astrologer reported: 'Mars was in Paogua and suddenly vanished, its whereabouts unknown; by rule it ought to enter a state facing peril and ruin, first giving rise to children's songs and strange talk, and then carrying out its calamities and punishments.'
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer of Wei reported, 'Mars was in the Paogua asterism and suddenly vanished without trace. By astrological rule it should enter a state facing ruin, first stirring up children's songs and ominous rumors, then bringing down calamity and punishment.'

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣召名儒十餘人使與太史議熒惑所詣，崔浩對曰：「按《春秋左氏傳》，『神降於莘』，以其至之日推知其物。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si summoned more than ten eminent Confucians to discuss with the Grand Astrologer where Mars was bound; Cui Hao replied: 'According to the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, "A spirit descended at Shen"—from the day of its arrival one may infer what it portends.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si summoned more than ten eminent scholars to discuss with the Grand Astrologer where Mars was headed. Cui Hao replied, 'The Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says, "A spirit descended at Shen"—from the day of its arrival one may infer what it signifies.

sentences.zh: 庚午之夕，辛未之朝，天有陰雲；

translations.literal: On the evening of gengwu and the morning of xinwei, the sky had overcast clouds;
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of gengwu and the morning of xinwei the sky was overcast;

sentences.zh: 熒惑之亡，當在二日。

translations.literal: Mars's disappearance ought to have fallen within those two days.
translations.idiomatic: Mars must have vanished on one of those two days.

sentences.zh: 庚之與午，皆主於秦；

translations.literal: Both geng and wu are associated with Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Both geng and wu correspond to Qin;

sentences.zh: 辛為西夷。

translations.literal: xin stands for the western barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: xin corresponds to the western barbarians.

sentences.zh: 今姚興據長安，熒惑必入秦矣。」

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing holds Chang'an—Mars must enter Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing now holds Chang'an—Mars must be entering Qin.'

sentences.zh: 眾皆怒曰：「天上失星，人間安知所詣！」

translations.literal: All angrily said: 'When a star is lost in heaven, how can men on earth know where it is bound!'
translations.idiomatic: The assembly angrily protested, 'When a star vanishes in the heavens, how can men on earth know where it is headed!'

sentences.zh: 浩笑而不應。

translations.literal: Hao smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hao smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 後八十餘日，熒惑出東井，留守句己，久之乃去。

translations.literal: More than eighty days later, Mars emerged from Dongjing, remained stationary at Juji, and only after a long time departed.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty days later Mars reappeared in Dongjing, lingered at Juji, and only after a long interval moved on.

sentences.zh: 秦大旱，昆明池竭，童謠訛言，國人不安，間一歲而秦亡。

translations.literal: Qin suffered great drought; the Kunming Pool dried up; children's songs and false rumors spread; the people of the state were unsettled; within a year Qin perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qin suffered a severe drought, the Kunming Pool ran dry, children's songs and wild rumors spread, and the people grew restless. Within a year Qin fell.

sentences.zh: 眾乃服浩之精妙。

translations.literal: The assembly then submitted to the subtle precision of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly then acknowledged the subtle brilliance of Cui Hao's prediction.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬子，秦王興使散騎常侍姚敞等，送其女西平公主於魏，魏主嗣以後禮納之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renzi, Qin King Xing sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Yao Chang and others to escort his daughter, the Princess of Xiping, to Wei; the Wei ruler Si received her with the rites due an empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renzi, King Yao Xing sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Yao Chang and others to escort his daughter, the Princess of Xiping, to Wei. Emperor Si received her with the rites due an empress.

sentences.zh: 鑄金人不成，乃以為夫人，而寵甚。

translations.literal: Because casting the golden statue did not succeed, she was made a consort instead, yet was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Because the casting of the golden statue failed, she was made a consort instead, yet was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏主嗣如沮洳城；

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Wei ruler Si went to Juru City;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Emperor Si of Wei traveled to Juru City;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，還平城。

translations.literal: on guihai, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on guihai he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，復如豺山宮；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, he again went to the Chai Mountain Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, he again went to the Chai Mountain Palace;

sentences.zh: 庚子，還。

translations.literal: on gengzi, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: on gengzi he returned.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐遣襄武侯曇達等將騎一萬，擊南羌彌姐、康薄於赤水，降之；

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan sent Marquis of Xiangwu Tanda and others to lead ten thousand horsemen to attack the Southern Qiang Mijie and Kangbo at Chishui and received their surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Western Qin, sent the Marquis of Xiangwu, Tanda, and others at the head of ten thousand horsemen to attack the Southern Qiang leaders Mijie and Kangbo at Chishui and accepted their surrender;

sentences.zh: 以王孟保為略陽太守，鎮赤水。

translations.literal: he made Wang Mengbao Administrator of Lueyang to garrison Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Wang Mengbao governor of Lueyang to garrison Chishui.

sentences.zh: 燕尚書令孫護之弟伯仁為昌黎尹，與其弟叱支拔皆有才勇，從燕王跋起兵有功，求開府不得，有怨言，跋皆殺之。

translations.literal: Yan's Minister of the Masters of Writing Sun Hu's younger brother Boren was Magistrate of Changli; he and his younger brother Chizhiba both had talent and courage, followed Yan King Ba in raising troops with merit, sought the privilege of opening a headquarters but did not obtain it, and harbored complaints—Ba had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Boren, younger brother of Sun Hu, Minister of the Masters of Writing of Yan, was magistrate of Changli. He and his younger brother Chizhiba were both talented and brave, had followed King Murong Ba in raising troops with distinction, and sought permission to open a headquarters but were refused. Nursing grievances, they were all put to death by Ba.

sentences.zh: 進護開府儀同三司、錄尚書事，以慰其心，護怏怏不悅，跋鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Hu was promoted to the privilege of opening a headquarters with the ceremonial parity of the Three Excellencies and made Recorder of the Masters of Writing to soothe his heart, but Hu was discontented and unhappy, and Ba poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hu was promoted to the privilege of opening a headquarters with ceremonial parity of the Three Excellencies and appointed Recorder of the Masters of Writing to appease him, but Hu remained sullen and dissatisfied, and Ba had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守務銀提自以有功，出為邊郡，怨望，謀外叛，跋亦殺之。

translations.literal: Liaodong Administrator Wuyinti, believing himself meritorious yet sent out to a frontier commandery, nursed resentment and plotted to defect abroad—Ba killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyinti, governor of Liaodong, felt he deserved better than assignment to a frontier commandery. Nursing resentment, he plotted to defect abroad, and Ba had him killed as well.

sentences.zh: 林邑寇交州，州將擊敗之。

translations.literal: Linyi raided Jiao Province, and the provincial commander defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi raided Jiao Province, and the provincial commander repulsed the attack.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝壬義熙十二年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, ren year, twelfth year of the Yixi era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, ren year, twelfth year of the Yixi era (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元四一六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, AD 416)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, AD 416)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，魏主嗣如豺山宮。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, the Wei ruler Si went to the Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on jiashen, Emperor Si of Wei traveled to the Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊子，還平城。

translations.literal: On wuzi, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 加太尉裕兗州刺吏、都督南秦州，凡都督二十二州；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu was additionally made Governor of Yan Province and Commander-in-Chief of Southern Qin Province, commanding twenty-two provinces in all;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu was additionally appointed Governor of Yan Province and Commander-in-Chief of Southern Qin Province, with authority over twenty-two provinces in all;

sentences.zh: 以世子義符為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: the heir Yifu was made Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: his heir Liu Yifu was appointed Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 秦王興使魯宗之將兵寇襄陽，未至而卒。

translations.literal: Qin King Xing sent Lu Zongzhi to lead troops to raid Xiangyang, but before he arrived he died.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing sent Lu Zongzhi to raid Xiangyang with an army, but Zongzhi died before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 其子軌引兵入寇，雍州刺史趙倫之擊敗之。

translations.literal: His son Gui led troops in to raid; Yong Province Inspector Zhao Lunzhi defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui led troops across the border to raid, and Zhao Lunzhi, Governor of Yong Province, defeated him.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐攻秦洮陽公彭利和於漒川，沮渠蒙遜攻石泉以救之。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Chipan attacked Qin's Duke of Taoyang Peng Lihe at Qiangchuan; Juqu Mengsun attacked Shiquan to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, King of Western Qin, attacked Peng Lihe, Duke of Taoyang of Qin, at Qiangchuan; Juqu Mengsun attacked Shiquan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 熾磐至沓中，引還。

translations.literal: Chipan reached Tazhong and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan reached Tazhong and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二月，熾磐遣襄武侯曇達救石泉，蒙遜亦引去。

translations.literal: In the second month, Chipan sent Marquis of Xiangwu Tanda to rescue Shiquan, and Mengsun also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Chipan sent the Marquis of Xiangwu, Tanda, to relieve Shiquan, and Mengsun withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遂與熾磐結和親。

translations.literal: Mengsun then formed a marriage alliance with Chipan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun then sealed a marriage alliance with Chipan.

sentences.zh: 秦王興如華陰，使太子泓監國，入居西宮。

translations.literal: Qin King Xing went to Huayin, had Crown Prince Hong oversee the state, and entered the Western Palace to reside.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing traveled to Huayin, left Crown Prince Yao Hong to govern the state, and took up residence in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 興疾篤，還長安，黃門侍郎尹沖謀因泓出迎而殺之。

translations.literal: When Xing's illness grew grave and he returned to Chang'an, Yellow Gate Attendant Yin Chong plotted to kill Hong when he came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing's illness grew critical and he returned to Chang'an, Yellow Gate Attendant Yin Chong plotted to kill Hong when the crown prince came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 興至，泓將出迎，宮臣諫曰：「主上疾篤，奸臣在側，殿下今出，進不得見主上，退有不測之禍。」

translations.literal: When Xing arrived, Hong was about to go out to welcome him; palace officials remonstrated, saying: 'The sovereign's illness is grave and treacherous ministers are at his side; if Your Highness goes out now, advancing you will not be able to see the sovereign, and retreating will bring unforeseen disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xing arrived, Hong was about to go out to welcome him. Palace officials remonstrated, 'The sovereign's illness is grave and treacherous ministers stand at his side. If Your Highness goes out now, you may not reach your father—and on your return you may meet disaster.'

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「臣子聞君父疾篤而端居不出，何以自安！」

translations.literal: Hong said: 'As subject and son, if I hear that my lord and father is gravely ill yet sit upright at home and do not go out, how can I be at ease!'
translations.idiomatic: Hong replied, 'As son and subject, how can I sit at ease at home when I hear that my lord and father is gravely ill!'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「全身以安社稷，孝之大者也。」

translations.literal: They replied: 'To preserve one's person in order to secure the altars of soil and grain is the greatest filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: They answered, 'Preserving yourself to secure the state is the highest form of filial piety.'

sentences.zh: 泓乃止。

translations.literal: Hong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then stayed where he was.

sentences.zh: 尚書姚沙彌謂尹沖曰；

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Yao Shami said to Yin Chong:
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shami, Minister of the Masters of Writing, said to Yin Chong:

sentences.zh: 「太子不出迎，宜奉乘輿幸廣平公第；

translations.literal: "The crown prince does not come out to welcome him; the imperial carriage ought to be escorted to the residence of the Duke of Guangping;
translations.idiomatic: "The crown prince has not come out to welcome him. The imperial carriage should be taken to the residence of the Duke of Guangping;

sentences.zh: 宿衛將士聞乘輿所在，自當來集，太子誰與守乎！

translations.literal: When the palace guard soldiers hear where the imperial carriage is, they will naturally come and assemble; with whom will the crown prince hold the palace!
translations.idiomatic: Once the palace guards learn where the imperial carriage is, they will rally of their own accord—who will remain with the crown prince to hold the palace!

sentences.zh: 且吾屬以廣平公之故，已陷名逆節，將何所自容！

translations.literal: Moreover, our group, because of the Duke of Guangping, has already fallen under the name of treason and disloyalty; where shall we find a place for ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because of the Duke of Guangping we have already been branded traitors—where could we possibly find a footing now!

sentences.zh: 今奉乘輿以舉事，乃杖大順，不惟救廣平之禍，吾屬前罪亦盡雪矣。」

translations.literal: Now, if we escort the imperial carriage to raise our enterprise, we will be relying on the great rightful principle; not only will we rescue the Duke of Guangping from disaster, our group's former crimes will also be wholly cleared."
translations.idiomatic: If we now take the imperial carriage and act in its name, we will be standing on the highest lawful ground—not only saving the Duke of Guangping, but clearing all our past guilt as well."

sentences.zh: 沖以興死生未可知，欲隨興入宮作亂，不用沙彌之言。

translations.literal: Chong, because Xing's life or death was still uncertain, wished to follow Xing into the palace to raise a rebellion and did not accept Shami's words.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong, uncertain whether Yao Xing would live or die, wanted to follow him into the palace and launch a coup; he rejected Yao Shami's advice.

sentences.zh: 興入宮，命太子泓錄尚書事，東平公紹及右衛將軍胡翼度典兵禁中，防制內外。

translations.literal: Xing entered the palace, ordered Crown Prince Hong to record affairs of the Masters of Writing, and had the Duke of Dongping Shao and Right Guard General Hu Yidu command troops within the forbidden precinct to control inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing entered the palace, appointed Crown Prince Yao Hong recorder of the Masters of Writing, and put the Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, and Right Guard General Hu Yidu in charge of troops in the inner precinct to secure the palace and its approaches.

sentences.zh: 遣殿中上將軍斂曼嵬收弼等中甲仗，內之武庫。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Attendant Senior General Lian Manwei to collect the armor and weapons from Bi and the others in the palace and store them in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant Senior General Lian Manwei to seize the arms and armor of Yao Bi and his associates within the palace and deposit them in the arsenal.

sentences.zh: 興疾轉篤，其妹南安長公主問疾，不應。

translations.literal: Xing's illness turned increasingly grave; his younger sister, the Princess of Nan'an the Greater, inquired after his illness, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao Xing's illness worsened, his younger sister, the Princess of Nan'an the Greater, came to inquire after him, but he gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 幼子耕兒出，告其兄南陽公愔曰：「上已崩矣，宜速決計！」

translations.literal: His youngest son Geng'er came out and told his elder brother, the Duke of Nanyang Yin, saying: 'The sovereign has already died; you ought to decide quickly!'
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Geng'er came out and told his elder brother, the Duke of Nanyang, Yao Yin, 'The sovereign is already dead—you must act at once!'

sentences.zh: 愔即與尹沖帥甲士攻端門，斂曼嵬，胡翼度等勒兵閉門拒戰。

translations.literal: Yin immediately joined with Yin Chong to lead armored soldiers in attacking the Duan Gate; Lian Manwei, Hu Yidu, and the others marshaled troops, closed the gate, and resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin at once joined Yin Chong and led armored men in an assault on the Duan Gate. Lian Manwei, Hu Yidu, and others mustered troops, shut the gates, and fought them off.

sentences.zh: 愔等遣壯士登門，緣屋而入，及於馬道。

translations.literal: Yin and the others sent strong men to climb the gate, enter along the rooftops, and reach the horse ramp.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and his men sent warriors up onto the gate, then along the rooftops until they reached the horse ramp.

sentences.zh: 泓侍疾在咨議堂，太子右衛率姚和都帥東宮兵入屯馬道南。

translations.literal: Hong was attending to the illness in the Consultation Hall; the crown prince's Right Guard Leader Yao He Du led Eastern Palace troops in to encamp south of the horse ramp.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was attending his father in the Consultation Hall when Yao He Du, Right Guard Leader of the Eastern Palace, led crown prince's troops in and encamped south of the horse ramp.

sentences.zh: 愔等不得進，遂燒端門。

translations.literal: Yin and the others could not advance, and so set fire to the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to break through, Yin and his party set fire to the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 興力疾臨前殿，賜弼死。

translations.literal: Xing, forcing himself despite his illness, came before the front hall and granted Bi death.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning his last strength, Yao Xing appeared in the front hall and ordered Yao Bi to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 禁兵見興，喜躍，爭進赴賊，賊眾驚擾，和都以東宮兵自後擊之愔等大敗。

translations.literal: The palace guard troops, seeing Xing, rejoiced and leaped forward, vying to rush at the rebels; the rebel band was thrown into panic and confusion, and He Du, with the Eastern Palace troops, struck Yin and his party from the rear—they suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards, seeing Yao Xing, erupted in joy and surged forward against the rebels. The rebel force panicked, and He Du struck Yin and his men from the rear with Eastern Palace troops—they were routed utterly.

sentences.zh: 愔逃於驪山，其黨建康公呂隆奔雍，尹沖及弟泓來奔。

translations.literal: Yin fled to Mount Li; his partisan, the Duke of Jiankang Lü Long, fled to Yong; Yin Chong and his younger brother Hong came and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin fled to Mount Li; his ally the Duke of Jiankang, Lü Long, fled to Yong; Yin Chong and his younger brother Yao Hong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 興引東平公紹及妙贊、梁喜、尹昭、斂曼嵬入內寢，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: Xing summoned the Duke of Dongping Shao together with Miao Zan, Liang Xi, Yin Zhao, and Lian Manwei into the inner bedchamber and received their acceptance of the deathbed edict to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing summoned the Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, together with Miao Zan, Liang Xi, Yin Zhao, and Lian Manwei to his bedside and entrusted them with a deathbed edict to govern as regents.

sentences.zh: 明日，興卒。

translations.literal: The next day, Xing died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yao Xing died.

sentences.zh: 泓秘不發喪，捕南陽公愔及呂隆、大將軍尹元等，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Hong kept the death secret and did not announce mourning; he arrested the Duke of Nanyang Yin together with Lü Long, Grand General Yin Yuan, and the others, and all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong concealed the death and withheld the mourning announcement, then arrested the Duke of Nanyang, Yao Yin, Lü Long, Grand General Yin Yuan, and others—all were executed.

sentences.zh: 乃發喪，即皇帝位，大赦，改元永和。

translations.literal: He then announced the mourning, immediately ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he announce the mourning, ascend the throne, proclaim a general amnesty, and change the era name to Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 泓命齊公恢殺安定太守呂超，恢猶豫久之，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Hong ordered the Duke of Qi Hui to kill the Administrator of Anding Lü Chao; Hui hesitated for a long time before killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong ordered the Duke of Qi, Yao Hui, to kill Lü Chao, administrator of Anding; Hui hesitated for a long while before carrying out the order.

sentences.zh: 泓疑恢有貳心，恢由是懼，陰聚兵謀作亂。

translations.literal: Hong suspected that Hui had a divided heart; Hui therefore grew fearful and secretly gathered troops plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong suspected Yao Hui of disloyalty; Hui, alarmed, secretly gathered troops and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 泓葬興於偶陵，謚曰文桓皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: Hong buried Xing at Ouling, posthumously titled him Emperor Wenhuang, and gave him the temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong buried Yao Xing at Ouling, posthumously titled him Emperor Wenhuang, and gave him the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 初，興徙李平羌三千戶於安定。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xing had moved three thousand households of the Liping Qiang to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yao Xing had relocated three thousand Liping Qiang households to Anding.

sentences.zh: 興卒。

translations.literal: Xing died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing died.

sentences.zh: 羌酋黨容叛，泓遣撫軍將軍姚贊討降之，徙其酋豪於長安，餘遣還李閏，北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛，東平公紹討禽之。

translations.literal: The Qiang chieftain Dang Rong rebelled; Hong sent Pacifying Army General Yao Zan to attack and subdue him, moved the chieftains and magnates to Chang'an, and sent the remainder back to Li Run; the Administrator of Beidi Mao Yong seized Zhao's Stockade and rebelled, and the Duke of Dongping Shao attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain Dang Rong rebelled. Yao Hong sent Pacifying Army General Yao Zan to subdue him, relocated the tribal leaders to Chang'an, and sent the rest back to Li Run. Mao Yong, administrator of Beidi, seized Zhao's Stockade and rose in revolt; the Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 時姚宣鎮李閏，參軍韋宗聞毛雍叛，說宣曰：「主上新立，威德未著，國家之難，未可量也，殿下不可不為深慮。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xuan was garrisoned at Li Run; staff officer Wei Zong, hearing of Mao Yong's rebellion, urged Xuan, saying: 'The sovereign has newly ascended and his authority and virtue are not yet established; the state's troubles cannot be measured; Your Highness cannot fail to think deeply about this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao Xuan held Li Run. When staff officer Wei Zong heard of Mao Yong's rebellion, he urged Xuan, 'The new sovereign's authority is not yet established and the realm's troubles are incalculable. Your Highness must think carefully about what lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 邢望險要，宜徙據之，此霸王之資也。」

translations.literal: Xingwang is strategically vital; you ought to move and occupy it—this is capital for hegemony and kingship.'
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang is a strong strategic position. You should relocate there—it would be the foundation for empire.'

sentences.zh: 宣從之，帥戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。

translations.literal: Xuan followed this advice, leading thirty-eight thousand households, abandoned Li Run, and withdrew south to hold Xingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan took his advice, leading thirty-eight thousand households away from Li Run to fortify Xingwang in the south.

sentences.zh: 諸羌據李閏以叛，東平公紹進討破之。

translations.literal: The various Qiang occupied Li Run and rebelled; the Duke of Dongping Shao advanced to attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Various Qiang bands seized Li Run and rebelled; the Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, marched against them and broke their resistance.

sentences.zh: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹殺之。

translations.literal: Xuan went to Shao to surrender and accept blame; Shao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to surrender and accept punishment; Shao had him executed.

sentences.zh: 二月，加太尉裕中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the second month, Grand Commandant Yu was additionally made Grand Commander over all affairs at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Grand Commandant Liu Yu was additionally invested as supreme commander over all military affairs at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 裕戒嚴將伐秦。

translations.literal: Yu declared martial law and was about to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu put the army on alert and prepared to march against Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 詔加裕領司、豫二州刺史，以其世子義符為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict additionally made Yu concurrently Governor of Si and Yu Provinces, and appointed his heir Yifu Governor of Xu and Yan Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict additionally appointed Liu Yu concurrent governor of Si and Yu provinces and made his heir Liu Yifu governor of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王德文請啟行戌路，修敬山陵；

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye, Dewen, requested permission to set out on the garrison route and perform rites of respect at the imperial tombs;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dewen, Prince of Langye, asked leave to travel the garrison route and pay respects at the imperial tombs;

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: an edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: an edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬子，魏大赦，改元泰常。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day renzi, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taichang.

sentences.zh: 西秦襄武候曇達等擊秦秦州刺史姚艾於上邽，破之，徙其民五千餘戶於枹罕。

translations.literal: Western Qin's Marquis of Xiangwu Tanda and others attacked Qin's Governor of Qin Province Yao Ai at Shanggui, defeated him, and moved more than five thousand of his households to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda, Marquis of Xiangwu of Western Qin, attacked Yao Ai, governor of Qin province for Later Qin, at Shanggui, routed him, and relocated more than five thousand households to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸巳，加太尉裕領北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guisi, Grand Commandant Yu was additionally made Governor of North Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day guisi, Grand Commandant Liu Yu was additionally appointed governor of North Yong province.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，魏主嗣北巡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the Wei ruler Si toured the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day dingsi, the Wei emperor Tuoba Si toured the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 并州胡數萬落叛秦，入於平陽，推匈奴曹弘為大單于，攻立義將軍姚成都於匈奴堡。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of households of the Hu of Bing Province rebelled against Qin, entered Pingyang, and raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as Grand Chanyu; they attacked General Who Establishes Righteousness Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Xianbei households in Bing province rebelled against Later Qin, entered Pingyang, and proclaimed the Xiongnu Cao Hong Grand Chanyu; they besieged General Who Establishes Righteousness Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu Fort.

sentences.zh: 征東將軍姚懿自蒲阪討之，執弘，送長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。

translations.literal: Eastern Campaign General Yao Yi marched from Puban to attack them, seized Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand households of the powerful and prominent to Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Campaign General Yao Yi marched from Puban against them, captured Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and relocated fifteen thousand leading households to Yong province.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊盛攻秦祁山，拔之，進逼秦州。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Sheng attacked Qin's Qishan, took it, and advanced to press Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, king of the Di, attacked Qishan in Later Qin territory, captured it, and pressed toward Qin province.

sentences.zh: 秦後將軍姚平救之，盛引兵退；

translations.literal: Qin's Rear General Yao Ping came to rescue it, and Sheng withdrew his troops;
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin's Rear General Yao Ping came to the rescue, and Yang Sheng withdrew;

sentences.zh: 平與上邽守將姚嵩追之。

translations.literal: Ping together with the defending general of Shanggui, Yao Song, pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ping and Yao Song, the garrison commander at Shanggui, pursued him.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃帥騎四萬襲上邽，未至，嵩與盛戰於竹嶺，敗死。
