translations.literal: Xia King Bobo led forty thousand horsemen in a raid on Shanggui; before he arrived, Song fought Sheng at Zhuling and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo, king of Xia, led forty thousand cavalry in a surprise attack on Shanggui. Before he arrived, Yao Song fought Yang Sheng at Zhuling and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 勃勃攻上邽二旬，克之，殺秦州刺史姚軍都及將士五千餘人，因毀其城。

translations.literal: Bobo attacked Shanggui for twenty days, took it, killed Qin Province Governor Yao Jundu and more than five thousand officers and soldiers, and then destroyed the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo besieged Shanggui for twenty days, took it, killed Yao Jundu, governor of Qin province, along with more than five thousand officers and men, and razed the city.

sentences.zh: 進攻陰密，又殺秦將姚良子及將士萬餘人；

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Yinmi and again killed Qin general Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Yinmi, killing the Later Qin general Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand troops;

sentences.zh: 以其子昌為雍州刺史，鎮陰密。

translations.literal: he appointed his son Chang Governor of Yong Province and garrisoned him at Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed his son Chang governor of Yong province and stationed him at Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍姚恢棄安定，奔還長安，安定人胡儼等帥戶五萬據城降於夏。

translations.literal: Northern Campaign General Yao Hui abandoned Anding and fled back to Chang'an; the men of Anding, Hu Yan and others, leading fifty thousand households, held the city and surrendered to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Campaign General Yao Hui abandoned Anding and fled to Chang'an; Hu Yan and other local leaders, with fifty thousand households, held the city and surrendered to Xia.

sentences.zh: 勃勃使鎮東將軍羊苟兒將鮮卑五千鎮安定，進攻秦鎮西將軍姚諶於雍城，諶委鎮奔長安。

translations.literal: Bobo sent Eastern Garrison General Yang Gou'er to lead five thousand Xianbei to garrison Anding, and advanced to attack Qin's Western Garrison General Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen abandoned the garrison and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo sent Eastern Garrison General Yang Gou'er with five thousand Xianbei to hold Anding, then attacked Western Garrison General Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen abandoned his post and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 勃勃據雍，進掠郿城。

translations.literal: Bobo occupied Yong and advanced to plunder Meicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo seized Yong and pushed forward to raid Meicheng.

sentences.zh: 秦東平公紹及征虜將軍尹昭等將步騎五萬擊之，勃勃退趨安定，胡儼閉門拒之，殺羊苟兒及所將鮮卑，復以安定降秦。

translations.literal: Qin's Duke of Dongping Shao and Captive-Pacifying General Yin Zhao and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him; Bobo withdrew toward Anding; Hu Yan closed the gates and refused him entry, killed Yang Gou'er and the Xianbei he commanded, and again surrendered Anding to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, and Captive-Pacifying General Yin Zhao led fifty thousand foot and horse against him. Bobo fell back toward Anding, but Hu Yan shut the gates against him, killed Yang Gou'er and his Xianbei force, and surrendered Anding once more to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 紹進擊勃勃於馬鞍阪，破之，追至朝那，不及而還。

translations.literal: Shao advanced to attack Bobo at Ma'an Slope, defeated him, pursued him to Chaona, failed to overtake him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shao attacked Bobo at Ma'an Slope, routed him, and pursued as far as Chaona before turning back without catching him.

sentences.zh: 勃勃歸杏城。

translations.literal: Bobo returned to Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo withdrew to Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 楊盛復遣兄子倦擊秦，至陳倉，秦斂曼嵬擊卻之。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng again sent his elder brother's son Juan to attack Qin; reaching Chencang, Qin's Lian Manwei attacked and repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng again sent his nephew Juan against Later Qin; when he reached Chencang, Lian Manwei drove him back.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃復遣兄提南侵洩陽，秦車騎將軍姚裕等擊卻之。

translations.literal: Xia King Bobo again sent his elder brother Ti south to invade Xieyang; Qin's Chariots and Cavalry General Yao Yu and others attacked and repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo again sent his elder brother Ti south against Xieyang; Chariots and Cavalry General Yao Yu and others beat him back.

sentences.zh: 涼司馬索承明上書勸涼公暠伐河西王蒙遜，暠引見，謂之曰：「蒙遜為百姓患，孤豈忘之？

translations.literal: Liang's marshal Suo Chengming submitted a memorial urging the Duke of Liang Gao to attack the King of Hexi Mengsun; Gao summoned him for an audience and said to him: 'Mengsun is a scourge to the people—would I forget that?
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chengming, marshal of Liang, submitted a memorial urging Li Gao, Duke of Liang, to attack Mengsun, king of Hexi. Gao received him and said, 'Mengsun is a plague on the people—do you think I have forgotten that?

sentences.zh: 顧勢力未能除耳。

translations.literal: I only fear that my strength is not yet sufficient to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: I simply lack the strength to remove him yet.

sentences.zh: 卿有必禽之策，當為孤陳之；

translations.literal: If you have a strategy that is certain to capture him, you ought to set it forth for me;
translations.idiomatic: If you have a plan that will surely bring him down, lay it out for me;

sentences.zh: 直唱大言，使孤東討，此與言『石虎小豎，宜肆諸市朝』者何異！」

translations.literal: to speak grand words outright and make me march east to attack—how is this different from saying 'Shi Hu is a petty upstart who ought to be torn apart in the marketplace'!'
translations.idiomatic: but to talk big and tell me to march east—that is no different from saying 'Shi Hu is a petty upstart who ought to be torn apart in the marketplace'!'

sentences.zh: 承明慚懼而退。

translations.literal: Chengming, ashamed and fearful, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chengming withdrew in shame and alarm.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏主嗣大獵於牛川，臨殷繁水而還。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Wei ruler Si held a great hunt at Niuchuan, came to the Yinfan River, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Wei emperor Tuoba Si held a great hunt at Niuchuan, reached the Yinfan River, and returned.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，至平城。

translations.literal: On wuxu, he reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu he reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day bingwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 寧州獻琥珀枕於太尉裕。

translations.literal: Ning Province presented an amber pillow to Grand Commandant Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ning province presented an amber pillow to Grand Commandant Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕以琥珀治金創，得之大喜，命碎搗分賜北征將士。

translations.literal: Yu, because amber treats metal wounds, was greatly delighted on receiving it and ordered it crushed and pounded and distributed among the northern expedition officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that amber was used to treat metal wounds, Liu Yu was delighted and ordered it ground up and distributed among the troops on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 裕以世子義符為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: Yu made his heir Yifu Central Army General to oversee the affairs left at the Grand Commandant's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu appointed his heir Liu Yifu Central Army General to oversee affairs at the headquarters he was leaving behind.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi became Left Vice Director and concurrently served as army secretary of the Supervisory Army and Central Army headquarters, entered and resided in the Eastern Headquarters, and took overall charge of inside and outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director and concurrently army secretary of the Supervisory Army and Central Army headquarters; he moved into the Eastern Headquarters and took overall charge of internal and external affairs.

sentences.zh: 以太尉左司馬東海徐羨之為穆之之副，左將軍朱齡石守衛殿省，徐州刺史劉懷慎守衛京師，揚州別駕從事史張裕任留州事。

translations.literal: He made Grand Commandant Left Army Major Xu Xianzhi of Donghai Muzhi's deputy, Left General Zhu Lingshi guard the palace precinct, Xu Province Inspector Liu Huaishan guard the capital, and Yang Province Assistant Administrator Zhang Yu take charge of affairs left in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He made Grand Commandant Left Army Major Xu Xianzhi of Donghai Liu Muzhi's deputy, Left General Zhu Lingshi guardian of the palace precinct, Xu Province Inspector Liu Huaishan guardian of the capital, and Yang Province Assistant Administrator Zhang Yu administrator of affairs left behind in the province.

sentences.zh: 懷慎，懷敬之弟也。

translations.literal: Huaishan was the younger brother of Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaishan was the younger brother of Liu Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之內總朝政，外供軍旅，決斷如流，事無擁滯。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi internally commanded court governance and externally supplied the army; his decisions flowed like water and no affair was blocked or delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi directed court affairs at home and supplied the armies abroad; decisions flowed from him without delay or backlog.

sentences.zh: 賓客輻湊，求訴百端，內外咨稟，盈階滿室；

translations.literal: Guests and clients gathered like wheel spokes; petitions and appeals came from every direction; consultations and reports from inside and outside filled the steps and packed the rooms;
translations.idiomatic: Clients and petitioners crowded in from every direction; consultations and appeals from within and without filled the steps and packed the hall;

sentences.zh: 目鑒辭訟，手答箋書，耳行聽受，口並酬應，不相參涉，悉皆贍舉。

translations.literal: his eyes judged lawsuits, his hands answered letters and documents, his ears simultaneously listened and received, and his mouth answered in turn—without mutual interference, all were fully handled.
translations.idiomatic: his eyes judged lawsuits, his hands answered correspondence, his ears took in reports, and his mouth replied—all at once, without confusion, and nothing was left unattended.

sentences.zh: 又喜賓客，言談賞笑，彌日無倦。

translations.literal: He also delighted in guests, conversing, exchanging wit, and laughing throughout the day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved company, talking and laughing with guests from morning to night without tiring.

sentences.zh: 裁有閒暇，手自寫書，尋鑒校定。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a little leisure, he personally wrote books and sought out, examined, and corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: In whatever spare moments he had, he copied books by hand and collated them himself.

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，食必方丈，旦輒為十人饌，未嘗獨餐。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and grand; his meals always filled a square zhang, and each morning he had food prepared for ten people—he never dined alone.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant by nature, he never ate alone: every meal filled a square zhang of table, and each morning he had food laid for ten.

sentences.zh: 嘗白裕曰：「穆之家本貧賤，贍生多闕。

translations.literal: He once reported to Yu, saying: 'Muzhi's family was originally poor and lowly, and there were many gaps in making a living.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Liu Yu, 'My family was poor and humble, and I often lacked the means to live.

sentences.zh: 自叨忝以來，雖每存約損，而朝夕所須，微為過豐。

translations.literal: Since I have been favored with office, although I have each time kept to restraint and reduction, what is needed morning and evening is slightly over-abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Since receiving office I have tried to restrain myself, yet what I require day to day is still somewhat lavish.

sentences.zh: 自此外，一毫不以負公。」

translations.literal: Apart from this, not one hair's worth has been owed to the public.'
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, I have not taken so much as a hair's breadth from the public purse.'

sentences.zh: 中軍咨議參軍張邵言於裕曰：「人生危脆，必當遠慮。

translations.literal: Central Army Advisory Staff Officer Zhang Shao said to Yu: 'Human life is fragile and precarious; one must certainly think far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Advisory Staff Officer Zhang Shao said to Liu Yu, 'Life is fragile; one must plan for the long term.

sentences.zh: 穆之若邂逅不幸，誰可代之？

translations.literal: If Muzhi should by chance meet with misfortune, who could replace him?
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Muzhi should meet with sudden misfortune, who could replace him?

sentences.zh: 尊業如此。

translations.literal: Your great enterprise is as it is.
translations.idiomatic: Your great enterprise hangs on this.

sentences.zh: 苟有不諱，處分雲何？」

translations.literal: If there should be the unmentionable, how will affairs be disposed?'
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should happen, what arrangements have you made?'

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「此自委穆之及卿耳。」

translations.literal: Yu said: 'This I entrust to Muzhi and to you alone.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu replied, 'That I leave to Liu Muzhi and to you.'

sentences.zh: 丁巳，裕發建康，遣龍驤將軍王鎮惡、冠軍將軍檀道濟將步軍自淮、淝向許、洛，新野太守朱超石、寧朔將軍胡籓趨陽城，振武將軍沈田子、建威將軍傅弘之趨武關，建武將軍沈林子、彭城內史劉遵考將水軍出石門，自汴入河，以冀州刺史五仲德督前鋒諸軍，開巨野入河。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Yu set out from Jiankang, sent Dragon Cavalry General Wang Zhen'e and General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji to lead infantry from the Huai and Fei toward Xu and Luoyang, sent Xinye Administrator Zhu Chaoshi and General Who Pacifies the North Hu Fan toward Yangcheng, sent General Who Quells Martial Might Shen Tianzi and General Who Establishes Might Fu Hongzhi toward Wuguan, sent General Who Establishes Martial Might Shen Linzi and Pengcheng Interior Secretary Liu Zunkao to lead the navy out from Shimen and enter the Yellow River from the Bian, and had Governor of Ji Province Wang Zhongde supervise the vanguard armies, opening the route through Juye into the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi Liu Yu departed Jiankang. He sent Dragon Cavalry General Wang Zhen'e and General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji with infantry from the Huai and Fei toward Xu and Luoyang; Xinye Administrator Zhu Chaoshi and General Who Pacifies the North Hu Fan toward Yangcheng; General Who Quells Martial Might Shen Tianzi and General Who Establishes Might Fu Hongzhi toward Wuguan; General Who Establishes Martial Might Shen Linzi and Pengcheng Interior Secretary Liu Zunkao with the fleet out from Shimen into the Yellow River via the Bian; and Wang Zhongde, governor of Ji province, to command the vanguard and open the route through Juye into the river.

sentences.zh: 遵考，裕之族弟也。

translations.literal: Zunkao was Yu's clansman younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zunkao was Liu Yu's clansman younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之謂王鎮惡曰：「公今委卿以伐秦之任，卿其勉之！」

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi said to Wang Zhen'e: 'The lord now entrusts you with the task of attacking Qin; you must exert yourself!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi said to Wang Zhen'e, 'The lord now entrusts you with the conquest of Qin—give it your all!'

sentences.zh: 鎮惡曰：「吾不克關中，誓不復濟江！」

translations.literal: Zhen'e said: 'If I do not take Guanzhong, I swear never to cross the river again!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e replied, 'If I do not take Guanzhong, I swear never to cross the Yangzi again!'

sentences.zh: 裕既行，青州刺史檀祗自廣陵輒帥眾至塗中掩討亡命。

translations.literal: After Yu had set out, Qing Province Inspector Tan Zhi on his own authority from Guangling led troops to Tuzhong to surprise and suppress fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu had departed, Tan Zhi, inspector of Qing province, on his own authority led troops from Guangling to Tuzhong to hunt down fugitives.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之恐祗為變，議欲遣軍。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi feared that Zhi might turn mutinous and discussed sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi feared Tan Zhi might rebel and discussed dispatching troops against him.

sentences.zh: 時檀韶為江州刺史，張邵曰：「今韶據中流，道濟為軍首，若有相疑之跡，則大府立危，不如逆遣慰勞以觀其意，必無患也。」

translations.literal: At that time Tan Shao was Governor of Jiang Province; Zhang Shao said: 'Now Shao holds the middle reaches and Daoji is head of the army; if there are signs of mutual suspicion, the great headquarters will immediately be in peril—it would be better to send envoys ahead with words of comfort to observe his intentions; there will certainly be no trouble.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tan Shao was governor of Jiang province. Zhang Shao said, 'Shao holds the middle Yangzi and Daoji commands the army. Any sign of mutual suspicion would put the headquarters in immediate peril. Better to send envoys ahead with words of reassurance and watch his intentions—there will be no trouble.'

sentences.zh: 穆之乃止。

translations.literal: Muzhi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主嗣使公孫表討白亞栗斯，曰：「必先與秦洛陽戍將相聞，使備河南岸，然後擊之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei ruler Si sent Gongsun Biao to attack Bai Yalisi, saying: 'You must first inform the Qin garrison general at Luoyang and have him prepare the south bank of the river, and only then attack.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Wei emperor Tuoba Si sent Gongsun Biao against Bai Yalisi with orders, 'You must first notify the Later Qin garrison commander at Luoyang and have him ready the south bank of the Yellow River—only then strike.'

sentences.zh: 表未至，胡人廢白亞栗斯，更立劉虎為率善王。

translations.literal: Before Biao arrived, the Hu deposed Bai Yalisi and instead installed Liu Hu as King Who Leads in Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Before Biao arrived, the tribes deposed Bai Yalisi and installed Liu Hu as King Who Leads in Goodness.

sentences.zh: 表以胡人內自攜貳，勢必敗散，遂不告秦將而擊之，大為虎所敗，士卒死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Biao, because the Hu were internally divided and disloyal and were bound to be defeated and scatter, therefore did not inform the Qin general but attacked; he was greatly defeated by Hu, and officers and soldiers killed and wounded were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Biao judged that internal divisions among the tribes would doom them to collapse, so he attacked without notifying the Later Qin commander. Liu Hu routed him badly, with heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 嗣謀於群臣曰：「胡叛逾年，討之不克，其眾繁多，為患日深。

translations.literal: Si consulted his ministers, saying: "The Hu rebellion has lasted more than a year; attacking it we cannot overcome it; their numbers are vast and the harm grows deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Si consulted his ministers, saying, "The Hu rebellion has dragged on for more than a year. We cannot suppress it, their numbers are vast, and the threat grows worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 今盛秋不可復發兵，妨民農務，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Now in the height of autumn we cannot again send out troops and obstruct the people's agricultural work—what are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: It is high autumn and we cannot mobilize again without disrupting the harvest—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 白馬侯崔宏曰：「胡眾雖多，無健將御之，終不能成大患。

translations.literal: the Marquis of Baima Cui Hong said: 'Although the Hu are numerous, without a strong general to command them, in the end they cannot become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Baima, Cui Hong, said, 'The Hu are many, but without a capable commander they can never become a serious threat.

sentences.zh: 表等諸軍，不為不足，但法令不整，處分失宜，以致敗耳。

translations.literal: Biao's armies and the rest are not insufficient; it is only that the laws and orders are not disciplined and the disposition is inappropriate, so that defeat was brought about, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's forces are ample enough; the problem is undisciplined command and poor decisions, which is why they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 得大將素有威望者將數百騎往攝表軍，無不克矣。

translations.literal: If one obtains a great general who has long possessed prestige and leads several hundred horsemen to go and take command of Biao's army, there is none that would not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Send a seasoned general of established renown with a few hundred horsemen to take charge of Biao's troops, and success is assured.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史叔孫建前在并州，為胡、魏所畏服，諸將莫及，可遣也。」

translations.literal: The Governor of Xiang Province Shusun Jian, who formerly was in Bing Province, was feared and submitted to by the Hu and Wei; none of the generals could match him—he may be dispatched.'
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian, Governor of Xiang Province, once served in Bing Province and was feared by both the tribes and our own forces alike; no general compares—he is the man to send.'

sentences.zh: 嗣從之，以建為中領軍，督表等討虎。

translations.literal: Si followed this, appointing Jian as Central Palace Guard General and supervising Biao and the others in attacking Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Si agreed and made Shusun Jian Central Palace Guard General, putting him in command of Biao and the other generals against Liu Hu.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，大破之，斬首萬餘級，虎及司馬順宰皆死，俘其眾十萬餘口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuwu, he inflicted a great defeat; heads cut numbered more than ten thousand ranks; Hu and Sima Shunzai both died; he captured more than one hundred thousand of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuwu, he routed the rebels utterly, taking more than ten thousand heads. Liu Hu and Sima Shunzai were both killed, and over one hundred thousand of their followers were captured.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕至彭城，加領徐州刺史；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu arrived at Pengcheng and was additionally made concurrent Governor of Xu Province;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Pengcheng and was given the additional post of Governor of Xu Province;

sentences.zh: 以太原王玄謨為從事史。

translations.literal: he made Wang Xuannuo of Taiyuan a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Wang Xuannuo of Taiyuan as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 初，王廞之敗也，沙門曇永匿其幼子華，使提衣襆自隨，津邏疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Mi was defeated, the monk Tan Yong hid his young son Hua, making him carry bundles of clothing and follow along; the ferry patrol suspected them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Mi's defeat, the monk Tan Yong concealed Mi's young son Hua, having the boy carry bundles of clothing as they traveled. Ferry guards grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 曇永呵華曰：「奴子何不速行！」

translations.literal: Tan Yong shouted at Hua, saying, "You slave-boy—why don't you hurry along!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yong scolded Hua: "You worthless brat—why aren't you moving faster!"

sentences.zh: 棰之數十，由是得免；

translations.literal: and beat him several dozen times; by this they were able to escape;
translations.idiomatic: He thrashed him dozens of times. The ruse worked and they got away;

sentences.zh: 遇赦，還吳。

translations.literal: they encountered an amnesty and returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: after an amnesty was proclaimed, Hua returned to Wu.

sentences.zh: 以其父存亡不測，布蔬食，絕交遊不仕，十餘年。

translations.literal: Because his father's life or death was uncertain, he wore coarse cloth and ate plain food, cut off social ties and did not take office—for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: With his father's fate unknown, he lived in coarse dress on a vegetarian diet, withdrew from society, and refused office for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 裕聞華賢，欲用之，乃發廞喪，使華制服。

translations.literal: Yu heard that Hua was worthy and wished to employ him; he therefore announced Mi's death and had Hua put on mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, hearing of Hua's talent, wished to employ him. He had Mi's death formally announced and had Hua enter mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，闢為徐州主簿。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was summoned and made Chief Clerk of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, Hua was appointed Chief Clerk of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡、檀道濟入秦境，所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e and Tan Daoji entered Qin territory; wherever they went all was victory.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e and Tan Daoji crossed into Later Qin territory and met success wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 秦將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，諸屯守皆望風款附。

translations.literal: The Qin general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Zhen'e; the Governor of Xu Province Yao Zhang surrendered Xiangcheng to Daoji; all the garrison defenders submitted at the sight of their banners.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e; Yao Zhang, Governor of Xu Province, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji; garrison after garrison submitted without a fight.

sentences.zh: 惟新蔡太守董遵不下，道濟攻拔其城，執遵，殺之。

translations.literal: Only the Administrator of Xincai Dong Zun would not submit; Daoji attacked and took his city, seized Zun, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dong Zun, Administrator of Xincai, held out. Tan Daoji stormed the city, captured him, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 進克許昌，獲秦穎川太守姚垣及大將楊業。

translations.literal: Advancing, they captured Xuchang and took the Qin Governor of Yingchuan Yao Yuan and the great general Yang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to capture Xuchang, taking Yao Yuan, Governor of Yingchuan, and the great general Yang Ye.

sentences.zh: 沈林子自汴入河，襄邑人董神虎聚眾千餘人來降。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi entered the river from Bian; Dong Shenhu of Xiangyi gathered a crowd of more than a thousand men and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi entered the Yellow River from the Bian Canal. Dong Shenhu of Xiangyi rallied more than a thousand men and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕版為參軍。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu provisionally appointed him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu provisionally appointed him a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 林子與神虎共攻倉垣，克之，秦兗州刺史韋華降。

translations.literal: Linzi and Shenhu together attacked Cangyuan and took it; the Qin Governor of Yan Province Wei Hua surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi and Shenhu jointly attacked Cangyuan and took it. Wei Hua, Governor of Yan Province, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 神虎擅還襄邑，林子殺之。

translations.literal: Shenhu on his own authority returned to Xiangyi; Linzi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenhu withdrew to Xiangyi on his own authority. Linzi had him executed.

sentences.zh: 秦東平公紹言於秦主泓曰：「晉兵已過許昌，安定孤遠，難以救衛，宜遷其鎮戶，內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，雖晉、夏交侵，猶不亡國。

translations.literal: The Qin Duke of Dongping Shao spoke to the Qin ruler Hong, saying, "Jin troops have already passed Xuchang; Anding is isolated and distant and difficult to rescue or defend; it is fitting to move its garrison households inward to fill the capital region—one can obtain a hundred thousand elite troops; even if Jin and Xia invade together, the state will still not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao, Duke of Dongping, said to the Later Qin emperor Yao Hong: "The Jin army has already passed Xuchang. Anding is isolated and far away and cannot be saved. We should relocate its garrison households to strengthen the capital region and raise a hundred thousand elite troops. Even if Jin and Xia attack together, the state need not fall.

sentences.zh: 不然，晉攻豫州，夏攻安定，將若之何？

translations.literal: Otherwise, Jin will attack Yu Province and Xia will attack Anding—what are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Jin will strike Yu Province while Xia strikes Anding—what then?

sentences.zh: 事機已至，宜在速決。」

translations.literal: The moment of opportunity has arrived; one should act with swift decision.'
translations.idiomatic: The moment demands a swift decision."

sentences.zh: 左僕射梁喜曰：「劉公恢有威名，為嶺北所憚，鎮人已與勃勃深仇，理應守死無貳。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Liang Xi said, "Lord Liu Hui has a reputation for prestige and is feared north of the mountains; the garrison people already bear deep enmity toward Bobo and, by right, ought to hold to the death without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Liang Xi replied: "Liu Hui enjoys great prestige and is feared north of the Qinling range. The garrison people are sworn enemies of Helian Bobo and will hold Anding to the death.

sentences.zh: 勃勃終不能越安定遠寇京畿；

translations.literal: Bobo in the end cannot cross Anding to raid the capital region from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Bobo cannot bypass Anding to threaten the capital from afar;

sentences.zh: 若無安定，虜馬必至於郿。

translations.literal: if there is no Anding, the barbarian horses will surely reach Mei.
translations.idiomatic: without Anding as a shield, enemy horsemen will reach as far as Mei.

sentences.zh: 今關中兵足以拒晉，無為豫自損削也。」

translations.literal: Now the Guanzhong troops are sufficient to resist Jin; do not needlessly weaken ourselves in advance.'
translations.idiomatic: The forces in Guanzhong are enough to hold Jin at bay. We should not weaken ourselves needlessly."

sentences.zh: 泓從之。

translations.literal: Hong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong accepted this advice.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「恢於廣平之難，有忠勳於畢下。

translations.literal: The Director of the Ministry of Civil Service Yi Heng spoke secretly to Hong, saying, "At the crisis of Guangping, Hui had loyal merit before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Heng, a director in the Ministry of Civil Service, privately told Yao Hong: "At the crisis of Guangping, Liu Hui rendered loyal service to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞為答其意。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne and succeeded to the lineage, there has been no special reward to answer his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, he has received no special reward commensurate with that service.

sentences.zh: 今外則致之死地，內則不豫朝權，安定人自以孤危逼寇，思南遷者十室而九，若恢擁精兵數萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎！

translations.literal: Now outwardly he is placed in a land of death, inwardly he is not admitted to court power; the people of Anding themselves regard their isolation and peril and the pressing enemy—in nine houses out of ten they think of moving south; if Hui holds elite troops numbering in the tens of thousands and beats the drums marching toward the capital, can he fail to become a burden to the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Now he is left exposed to the enemy abroad while denied influence at court. The people of Anding feel isolated and imperiled; nine households in ten dream of fleeing south. If Liu Hui holds tens of thousands of elite troops and marches on the capital, will he not become a grave threat to the throne?

sentences.zh: 宜征還朝廷以慰其心。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to summon him back to court to comfort his heart.'
translations.idiomatic: He should be recalled to court to reassure him."

sentences.zh: 泓曰、「恢若懷不逞之心，征之適所以速禍耳。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "If Hui harbors a mind of discontent, summoning him would only hasten disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said, "If Liu Hui already harbors rebellious intent, recalling him would only hasten disaster."

sentences.zh: 又不從。

translations.literal: He again did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: He refused this advice as well.

sentences.zh: 王仲德水軍入河，將逼滑台。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongde's river fleet entered the river and was about to press upon Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde's fleet entered the Yellow River and advanced toward Huatai.

sentences.zh: 魏兗州刺史尉建畏懦，帥眾棄城，北渡河。

translations.literal: The Wei Governor of Yan Province Wei Jian was fearful and cowardly; he led his troops in abandoning the city and crossed the river northward.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian, Governor of Yan Province for Wei, lost his nerve, abandoned the city with his troops, and fled north across the river.

sentences.zh: 仲德入滑台，宣言曰：「晉本欲以布帛七萬匹假道於魏，不謂魏之守將棄城遽去。」

translations.literal: Zhongde entered Huatai and proclaimed, saying, "Jin originally intended to borrow passage through Wei with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk; we did not expect Wei's defending general to abandon the city and depart in haste.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde entered Huatai and announced: "Jin originally meant to pass through Wei with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk as payment. We never expected Wei's garrison commander to flee the city in such haste."

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣聞之，遣叔孫建、公孫表自河內向枋頭，因引兵濟河，斬尉建於城下，投屍於河。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si heard this and dispatched Shusun Jian and Gongsun Biao from Henei toward Fangtou; they then led troops across the river, beheaded Wei Jian beneath the city wall, and cast his corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Si heard of this, he sent Shusun Jian and Gongsun Biao from Henei toward Fangtou, crossed the river with their troops, beheaded Wei Jian beneath the walls, and threw his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 呼仲德軍人，問以侵寇之狀。

translations.literal: He summoned Wang Zhongde's soldiers and questioned them about the circumstances of invasion and raiding.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned soldiers from Wang Zhongde's force and questioned them about the incursion.

sentences.zh: 仲德使司馬竺和之對曰：「劉太尉使王征虜自河入洛，清掃山陵，非敢為寇於魏也。

translations.literal: Zhongde sent his staff officer Zhu Hezhi to reply, saying, "Grand Marshal Liu sent the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Wang to enter Luo from the river and sweep clean the imperial tombs; we do not dare to act as raiders against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde had his staff officer Zhu Hezhi reply: "Grand Marshal Liu sent General Wang to enter Luoyang by river to restore the imperial tombs. We have no intention of raiding Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏之守將自棄滑台去，王征虜借空城以息兵，行當西引，於晉、魏之好無廢也，何必揚旗鳴鼓以曜威乎！」

translations.literal: Wei's defending general on his own abandoned Huatai and left; the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians borrowed the empty city to rest the troops and will soon withdraw westward—the good relations between Jin and Wei are not abandoned; why must you raise banners and beat drums to display might!'
translations.idiomatic: Wei's commander abandoned Huatai of his own accord. General Wang merely occupied the empty city to rest his men and will soon withdraw westward. This in no way breaks the friendship between Jin and Wei—why raise banners and beat drums in a show of force?"

sentences.zh: 嗣使建以問太尉裕，裕遜辭謝之曰：「洛陽，晉之舊都，而羌據之；

translations.literal: Si had Jian go to question Grand Marshal Yu; Yu with deferential words apologized, saying, "Luoyang is Jin's former capital, yet the Qiang hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Si had Shusun Jian put the question to Grand Marshal Liu Yu. Liu Yu replied with elaborate courtesy: "Luoyang is Jin's ancient capital, yet the Qiang hold it;

sentences.zh: 晉欲修復山陵久矣。

translations.literal: Jin has long wished to restore the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin has long wished to restore the imperial tombs there.

sentences.zh: 諸醒宗族，司馬休之、國璠兄弟，魯宗之父子，皆晉之蠹也，而羌收之以為晉患。

translations.literal: The various clan kindreds—Sima Xiuzhi, the brothers Guofan, Lu Zongzhi and his son—all are Jin's parasites, yet the Qiang have taken them in and made them Jin's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clansmen—Sima Xiuzhi, the brothers Guofan, Lu Zongzhi and his son—are all parasites upon Jin, yet the Qiang have sheltered them and turned them into scourges against us.

sentences.zh: 今晉將伐之，欲假道於魏，非敢為不利也。」

translations.literal: Now Jin is about to attack them and wishes to borrow passage through Wei; we do not dare to act to Wei's harm.'
translations.idiomatic: Jin is now marching to punish them and merely seeks passage through Wei. We mean Wei no harm."

sentences.zh: 魏河內鎮將於栗磾有勇名，築壘於河上以備侵軼。

translations.literal: The Wei garrison commander of Henei Yu Libo had a reputation for bravery; he built fortifications on the river to guard against incursions and raids.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libo, Wei's garrison commander at Henei, was famed for his courage. He built fortifications along the river to guard against incursions.

sentences.zh: 裕以書與之，題曰「黑槊公麾下」。

translations.literal: Yu sent him a letter, addressing it "To the camp of the Lord of the Black Spear."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wrote to him, addressing the letter "To the camp of the Lord of the Black Spear."

sentences.zh: 栗磾好操黑槊以自標，故裕以此目之。

translations.literal: Libo liked to wield a black spear as his mark, so Yu used this to address him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libo was fond of carrying a black spear as his personal emblem, and Liu Yu addressed him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 魏因拜栗磾為黑槊將軍。

translations.literal: Wei thereupon enfeoffed Libo as General of the Black Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Wei thereupon created Yu Libo General of the Black Spear.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬戌，魏主嗣如豺山宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day renxu, the Wei ruler Si went to the Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor Tuoba Si went to the Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，燕將庫辱官斌降魏，既而復叛歸燕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Yan general Kuruguan Bin surrendered to Wei; afterward he again rebelled and returned to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Yan general Kuruguan Bin had surrendered to Wei, then rebelled and returned to Yan.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣遣驍騎將軍延普渡濡水擊斌，斬之；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si dispatched the Swift Cavalry General Yan Pu to cross the Ru River and attack Bin, beheading him;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Si sent Swift Cavalry General Yan Pu across the Ru River to attack Bin and beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 遂攻燕幽州刺史辱官昌、征北將軍庫辱官提，皆斬之。

translations.literal: he then attacked the Yan Governor of You Province Ruguan Chang and the General Who Pacifies the North Kuruguan Ti, beheading them both.
translations.idiomatic: then attacked Ruguan Chang, Governor of You Province, and Kuruguan Ti, General Who Pacifies the North, and beheaded them both.

sentences.zh: 秦陽城、滎陽二城皆降，晉兵進至成皋。

translations.literal: The Qin cities of Yangcheng and Xingyang both surrendered; Jin troops advanced to Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin cities of Yangcheng and Xingyang both surrendered, and the Jin army advanced to Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 秦征南將軍陳留公洸鎮洛陽，遣使求救於長安。

translations.literal: The Qin General Who Conquers the South, the Duke of Chenliu Guang, garrisoned Luoyang and sent envoys to beg rescue at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang, Duke of Chenliu and General Who Conquers the South, held Luoyang and sent envoys to Chang'an begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 秦主泓遣越騎校尉閻生帥騎三千救之，武衛將軍姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣并州牧姚懿南屯陝津，為之聲援。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Hong dispatched the Commandant of Swift Cavalry Yan Sheng to lead three thousand horsemen to rescue it; the Martial Guard General Yao Yinan led ten thousand foot soldiers to help defend Luoyang; he also dispatched the Governor of Bing Province Yao Yi to encamp south at Shanjin as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Commandant of Swift Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horsemen to the rescue, Martial Guard General Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to reinforce Luoyang, and Governor of Bing Province Yao Yi to encamp south at Shanjin as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍趙玄言於洸曰：「今晉寇益深，人情駭動，眾寡不敵，若出戰不捷，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Xuan spoke to Guang, saying, "Now the Jin invaders grow ever deeper; men's hearts are shaken with alarm; our numbers cannot match theirs; if we go out to battle and do not prevail, then the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Xuan said to Yao Guang: "The Jin invasion grows deeper by the day, morale is shaken, and we are outnumbered. If we take the field and lose, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 宜攝諸戍之兵，固守金墉，以待西師之救。

translations.literal: It is fitting to gather the troops of the various garrisons and firmly hold the Jinyong fortress, awaiting rescue from the western army.
translations.idiomatic: We should concentrate the garrison troops and hold the Jinyong fortress until relief arrives from the west.

sentences.zh: 金墉不下，晉必不敢越我而西，是我不戰而坐收其弊也。」

translations.literal: If Jinyong is not taken, Jin will surely not dare to pass us and go west—thus we receive their exhaustion without fighting.'
translations.idiomatic: As long as Jinyong holds, Jin will not dare march past us toward the west. We can wear them down without giving battle."

sentences.zh: 司馬姚禹陰與檀道濟通，主簿閻恢、楊虔，皆禹之黨也，共嫉玄，言於洸曰：「殿下以英武之略，受任方面；

translations.literal: The staff officer Yao Yu secretly communicated with Tan Daoji; the chief clerks Yan Hui and Yang Qian were all Yu's faction; together they envied Xuan and spoke to Guang, saying, "Your Highness, with heroic and martial strategy, received appointment over a region;
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Yao Yu was secretly in contact with Tan Daoji. Chief clerks Yan Hui and Yang Qian, all Yu's allies, envied Zhao Xuan and said to Yao Guang: "Your Highness, appointed to command a frontier province with your renowned martial prowess,

sentences.zh: 今嬰城示弱，得無為朝廷所責乎！」

translations.literal: now to hold the city and show weakness—will you not be blamed by the court!'
translations.idiomatic: would you now shut yourself in the city and show weakness? Will the court not hold you accountable?"

sentences.zh: 洸以為然，乃遣趙玄將兵千餘南守柏谷塢，廣武將軍石無諱東戍鞏城。

translations.literal: Guang thought this right; he then dispatched Zhao Xuan to lead more than a thousand troops south to guard the Bo Valley stockade, and the General of Broad Might Shi Wuhui east to garrison Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang agreed. He sent Zhao Xuan with more than a thousand men south to hold the Bo Valley stockade and General of Broad Might Shi Wuhui east to garrison Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 玄泣謂洸曰：「玄受三帝重恩，所守正有死耳。

translations.literal: Xuan wept and said to Guang, "Xuan has received heavy grace from three emperors; in what I hold there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan wept and told Yao Guang: "I have received great favor from three emperors. In holding this post I can do no less than die.

sentences.zh: 但明公不用忠臣之言，為奸人所誤，後必悔之。」

translations.literal: Only that my lord does not use the words of a loyal minister and is misled by wicked men—you will surely regret this afterward.'
translations.idiomatic: But my lord has rejected a loyal minister's counsel and let himself be misled by villains. You will regret this."

sentences.zh: 既而成皋、虎牢皆來降，檀道濟等長驅而進，無諱至石關，奔還。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chenggao and Hulao both came to surrender; Tan Daoji and the others drove straight forward; Wuhui reached Shiguan and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenggao and Hulao surrendered. Tan Daoji and the others marched unopposed. Shi Wuhui reached Shiguan and fled back.

sentences.zh: 龍驤司馬滎陽毛德祖與玄戰於柏谷，玄兵敗，被十餘創，據地大呼。

translations.literal: The Dragon Cavalry staff officer Mao Dezu of Xingyang fought with Xuan at Bo Valley; Xuan's army was defeated; he received more than ten wounds and, bracing himself on the ground, shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry staff officer Mao Dezu of Xingyang fought Zhao Xuan at Bo Valley. Xuan's force was routed. Wounded more than ten times, he braced himself on the ground and cried out.

sentences.zh: 玄司馬蹇鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾創已重，君宜速去！」

translations.literal: Xuan's staff officer Jian Jian braved the blades, embraced Xuan, and wept; Xuan said, "My wounds are already grave—you should quickly go!'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's aide Jian Jian rushed through the blades, embraced him, and wept. Xuan said: "My wounds are mortal. You must leave at once!"

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「將軍不濟，鑒去安之！」

translations.literal: Jian said, "If the general does not survive, where would Jian go!'
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied: "If you do not survive, sir, where can I go?"

sentences.zh: 與之皆死。

translations.literal: Both died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Both died together.

sentences.zh: 姚禹逾城奔道濟，甲子，道濟進逼洛陽。

translations.literal: Yao Yu crossed the wall and fled to Daoji; on the day jiazi, Daoji advanced and pressed upon Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu climbed over the wall and fled to Tan Daoji. On jiazi, Tan Daoji pressed on toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，洸出降。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Guang came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Yao Guang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 道濟獲秦人四千餘人，議者欲盡坑之以為京觀。

translations.literal: Daoji captured more than four thousand Qin men; those in council wished to bury them all alive to make a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji took more than four thousand Later Qin soldiers captive. Some urged executing them all to erect a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 道濟曰：「伐罪弔民，正在今日！」

translations.literal: Daoji said, "To punish the guilty and comfort the people—this is exactly today!'
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji said: "We march to punish the guilty and succor the people—that purpose is fulfilled today!"

sentences.zh: 皆釋而遣之。

translations.literal: He released them all and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 於是夷、夏感悅，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon both barbarians and Chinese were moved with joy; those who submitted were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians and Chinese alike were deeply moved, and multitudes came over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 閻生、姚益男未至，聞洛陽已沒，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan had not yet arrived; hearing that Luoyang had already fallen, they did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan had not yet arrived. Learning that Luoyang had fallen, they dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔遣兼司空高密王恢之修謁五陵，置守衛。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, an edict dispatched the Concurrent Minister of Works, the Prince of Gaomi Hui Zhi, to repair and visit the five tombs and establish guards.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, an edict dispatched Concurrent Minister of Works Hui Zhi, Prince of Gaomi, to restore and visit the five imperial tombs and post guards.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕以冠軍將軍毛修之為河南、河內二郡太守，行司州事，戍洛陽。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu made the Champion General Mao Xiuzhi Administrator of the two commanderies of Henan and Henei, acting in the affairs of Si Province, to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu appointed Champion General Mao Xiuzhi Administrator of Henan and Henei, acting Governor of Si Province, to garrison Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐使秦州刺史王松壽鎮馬頭，以逼秦之上邽。

translations.literal: The Western Qin king Chipan sent the Governor of Qin Province Wang Songshou to garrison Matou, to press upon Qin's Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan, king of Western Qin, posted Wang Songshou, Governor of Qin Province, at Matou to threaten Later Qin's Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲戌，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiaxu, the Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, the Wei emperor Tuoba Si returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕遣左長史王弘還建康，諷朝廷求九錫。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu dispatched his Left Chief Clerk Wang Hong back to Jiankang to hint to the court that he sought the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu sent his Left Chief Clerk Wang Hong back to Jiankang to signal the court that he expected the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 時劉穆之掌留任，而旨從北來，穆之由是愧懼發病。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Muzhi held charge of affairs left behind; but the intent came from the north, and Muzhi therefore, ashamed and fearful, fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was then in charge at the capital. When the message arrived from the north, shame and dread overcame him and he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 弘，珣之子也。

translations.literal: Hong was the son of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was the son of Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，詔以裕為相國、總百揆、揚州牧，封十郡為宋公，備九錫之禮，位在諸侯王上，領征西將軍、司、豫、北徐、雍四州刺史如故，裕辭不受。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, an edict made Yu Chancellor, Director of All Affairs, and Governor of Yang Province; enfeoffed ten commanderies as Duke of Song; provided the rites of the Nine Bestowals; rank above the feudal princes and kings; continuing as General Who Conquers the West and Governor of the four provinces of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong as before—Yu declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, an edict appointed Liu Yu Chancellor, Director of All Affairs, and Governor of Yang Province; enfeoffed him as Duke of Song over ten commanderies with the full rites of the Nine Bestowals, rank above all feudal lords, while retaining his posts as General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Si, Yu, Northern Xu, and Yong. Liu Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐遣使詣太尉裕，求擊秦以自效。

translations.literal: The Western Qin king Chipan dispatched envoys to Grand Marshal Yu, requesting to attack Qin to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan of Western Qin sent envoys to Grand Marshal Liu Yu offering to attack Later Qin in Jin's service.

sentences.zh: 裕拜熾磐平西將軍、河南公。

translations.literal: Yu enfeoffed Chipan as General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu created him General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 秦姚懿司馬孫暢說懿使襲長安，誅東平公紹，廢秦主泓而代之。

translations.literal: Yao Yi's staff officer Sun Chang persuaded Yi to raid Chang'an, execute the Duke of Dongping Shao, depose the Qin ruler Hong, and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chang, staff officer to Yao Yi, urged Yi to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, Duke of Dongping, depose Yao Hong, and seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 懿以為然，乃散谷以賜河北夷、夏，欲樹私恩。

translations.literal: Yi thought this right; he then distributed grain to bestow upon the barbarians and Chinese north of the river, wishing to establish private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi agreed and began distributing grain to the tribes and Chinese north of the Yellow River, seeking to buy personal loyalty.

sentences.zh: 左常侍張敞、侍郎左雅諫曰：「殿下以母弟居方面，安危休戚，與國同之。

translations.literal: The Left Attendant Zhang Chang and the Gentleman Attendant Zuo Ya remonstrated, saying, "Your Highness, as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother holding a regional post, in safety and peril, weal and woe, shares with the state;
translations.idiomatic: Left Attendant Zhang Chang and Gentleman Attendant Zuo Ya remonstrated: "Your Highness, as the emperor's own brother holding a frontier command, shares the state's fortunes for good or ill.

sentences.zh: 今吳寇內侵。

translations.literal: Now the Wu invaders penetrate inward.
translations.idiomatic: Jin invades from the east.

sentences.zh: 四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危，有如累卵。

translations.literal: Four provinces have toppled and fallen; western barbarians disturb the borders; Qin and Liang are overturned in defeat; the court's peril is like a pile of eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Four provinces have fallen, western enemies harry the frontier, Qin and Liang are in ruins—the throne totters like a stack of eggs.

sentences.zh: 谷者，國之本也，而殿下無故散之，虛損國儲，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Grain is the foundation of the state, yet Your Highness without cause disperses it, vainly depleting the state's stores—what are we to do?'
translations.idiomatic: Grain is the foundation of the state. To squander it without cause depletes the treasury—what then?"

sentences.zh: 懿怒，笞殺之。

translations.literal: Yi was angry and had them beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi flew into a rage and had them flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 泓聞之，召東平公紹，密與之謀。

translations.literal: Hong heard of this and summoned the Duke of Dongping Shao, secretly plotting with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong learned of this, he summoned Yao Shao, Duke of Dongping, and plotted with him in secret.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「懿性識鄙淺，從物推移。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Yi's nature and understanding are shallow and base; he follows things as they shift.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is shallow and easily swayed.

sentences.zh: 造此謀者，必孫暢也。

translations.literal: The one who devised this plot must be Sun Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The mastermind must be Sun Chang.

sentences.zh: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍將軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至，臣當遣懿帥河東見兵共禦晉師；

translations.literal: Only dispatch a swift messenger to summon Chang; send the General Who Pacifies the Army Zan to hold Shancheng; I shall go toward Tong Pass to direct all the armies; if Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I shall dispatch Yi to lead the available troops of Hedong to jointly resist the Jin army together;
translations.idiomatic: Send a fast courier to summon Sun Chang. Post General Who Pacifies the Army Zan at Shancheng. I shall take Tong Pass and direct all forces. If Chang obeys the summons, I will have Yi lead the troops of Hedong against the Jin army;

sentences.zh: 若不受詔命，便當聲其罪而討之。」

translations.literal: if he does not accept the edict's command, then one should proclaim his crimes and punish him.'
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses, proclaim his crimes and move against him.'

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「叔父之言，杜稷之計也。」

translations.literal: Hong said: 'My uncle's words are a plan for the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said, 'My uncle speaks for the good of the realm itself.'

sentences.zh: 乃遣姚贊及冠軍將軍司馬國璠、建義將軍□也玄屯陝津，武衛將軍姚驢屯潼關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan, and Establishing Righteousness General [—] Yexuan to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard General Yao Lü to garrison Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan, and Establishing Righteousness General [—] Yexuan to hold Shan Ford, while Martial Guard General Yao Lü garrisoned Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 懿遂舉兵稱帝，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡谷以給鎮人。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon raised troops and declared himself emperor, issuing proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, intending to transport the grain of the Xiongnu Fort to supply the garrison population.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi thereupon took up arms and declared himself emperor, sending proclamations through the provinces and commanderies and planning to move grain from the Xiongnu Fort to feed his garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 寧東將軍姚成都拒之，懿卑辭誘之，送佩刀為誓，成都不從。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-East General Yao Chengdu resisted him; Yi used humble words to entice him and sent a girdle knife as a pledge, but Chengdu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-East General Yao Chengdu opposed him. Yi tried to win him with humble pleas and sent a girdle dagger as a pledge of faith, but Chengdu refused.

sentences.zh: 懿遣驍騎將軍王國帥甲士數百攻成都，成都擊禽之，遣使讓懿曰：「明公以至親當重任，國危不能救，而更圖非望；

translations.literal: Yi dispatched Swift Cavalry General Wang Guo to lead several hundred armored soldiers against Chengdu; Chengdu attacked and captured him, then sent an envoy to reproach Yi, saying: 'You, sir, hold a weighty post as a close kinsman, yet when the state is in peril you cannot save it and instead pursue illegitimate ambitions;
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Swift Cavalry General Wang Guo with several hundred armored men against Chengdu. Chengdu defeated and captured him, then sent an envoy to rebuke Yi: 'You hold high office as a kinsman of the house, yet when the state is in peril you fail to save it and instead reach for what is not yours;

sentences.zh: 三祖之靈，其肯佐明公乎！

translations.literal: would the spirits of the three ancestors consent to aid you, sir!
translations.idiomatic: will the spirits of the three ancestors aid you in this!

sentences.zh: 成都將糾合義兵，往見明公於河上耳。」

translations.literal: Chengdu will gather righteous troops and come to meet you, sir, on the riverbank.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall rally loyal troops and meet you on the riverbank.'

sentences.zh: 於是傳檄諸城，諭以逆順，徵兵調食以討懿。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued proclamations to the cities, explaining loyalty and rebellion, and levied troops and grain to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent proclamations to the cities, explaining the difference between loyalty and treason, and raised troops and supplies to march against Yi.

sentences.zh: 懿亦發諸城兵，莫有應者，惟臨晉數千戶應懿。

translations.literal: Yi also mobilized troops from the cities, but none responded except several thousand households of Linjin, who answered Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi likewise called up troops from the cities, but none answered except a few thousand households at Linjin.

sentences.zh: 成都引兵濟河，擊臨晉叛者，破之。

translations.literal: Chengdu led troops across the river, attacked the rebels of Linjin, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu crossed the river, struck the Linjin rebels, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 鎮人安定郭純等起兵圍懿。

translations.literal: Guo Chun of Anding and others among the garrison population rose in arms and besieged Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chun of Anding and others among the garrison troops rose and besieged Yi.

sentences.zh: 東平公紹入蒲阪，執懿，誅孫暢等。

translations.literal: Prince of Dongping Shao entered Puban, seized Yi, and executed Sun Chang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dongping, Yao Shao, entered Puban, seized Yi, and executed Sun Chang and his associates.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏衛將軍安城孝元王叔孫俊卒。

translations.literal: In this year, Wei's Guard General, Prince Xiaoyuan of Ancheng, Shusun Jun, died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Shusun Jun, Guard General of Wei and Prince Xiaoyuan of Ancheng, died.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣甚惜之，謂其妻桓氏曰：「生同其榮，能沒同其戚乎？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si greatly mourned him and said to his wife Lady Huan: 'In life we shared glory—can we not in death share sorrow?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si of Wei grieved deeply for him and said to his wife Lady Huan, 'In life we shared his glory—can you not share his sorrow in death?'

sentences.zh: 桓氏乃縊而□焉。

translations.literal: Lady Huan thereupon hanged herself and [—].
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huan then hanged herself and followed him.

sentences.zh: 丁零翟猛雀驅略吏民，入白三間為亂；

translations.literal: The Dingling Di Zhai Mengque drove off officials and commoners and entered Bai Sanjian to raise rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Mengque of the Dingling Di drove off officials and commoners and entered Bai Sanjian in revolt;

sentences.zh: 魏內都大官河內張蒲與冀州刺史長孫道生討之。

translations.literal: Wei's Director of the Inner Court Zhang Pu of Henei and Ji Province Inspector Changsun Daosheng campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu of Henei, Director of the Inner Court of Wei, and Changsun Daosheng, Inspector of Ji Province, marched against them.

sentences.zh: 道生，嵩之從子也。

translations.literal: Daosheng was the son of Changsun Song's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was a nephew of Changsun Song.

sentences.zh: 道生欲進兵擊猛雀，蒲曰：「吏民非樂為亂，為猛雀所迫脅耳。

translations.literal: Daosheng wished to advance and attack Mengque; Pu said: 'The officials and commoners do not delight in rebellion—they are merely coerced by Mengque.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng wanted to advance and strike Mengque at once. Pu said, 'The officials and commoners do not wish to rebel; they are only forced by Mengque.

sentences.zh: 今不分別，並擊之，雖欲返善，其道無由，必同心協力，據險以拒官軍，未易猝平也。

translations.literal: If we do not distinguish among them now and strike all alike, though they may wish to return to goodness, they will have no way to do so; they will surely unite in heart and strength, hold the defiles, and resist the government army—not easily pacified in haste.
translations.idiomatic: If we make no distinction and attack them all together, those who might return to loyalty will have no way to do so. They will unite, hold the passes, and resist the government troops, and the rebellion will not be quickly crushed.

sentences.zh: 不如先遣使諭之，以不與猛雀同謀者皆不坐，則必喜而離散矣。」

translations.literal: It would be better first to send envoys to instruct them that all who did not plot with Mengque will not be punished; then they will surely rejoice and disperse.'
translations.idiomatic: Better to send envoys first and announce that all who did not join Mengque's plot will go unpunished. They will rejoice and scatter of their own accord.'

sentences.zh: 道生從之，降者數千家，使復舊業。

translations.literal: Daosheng followed this advice; several thousand households submitted and were allowed to resume their former livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng agreed. Several thousand households surrendered and were allowed to return to their former occupations.

sentences.zh: 猛雀與其黨百餘人出走，蒲等追斬猛雀首，左部沿書周幾窮討餘黨，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Mengque fled with more than a hundred of his followers; Pu and the others pursued and beheaded Mengque, while Left Department Secretary Zhou Ji hunted down the remaining partisans to the end and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Mengque fled with a little more than a hundred followers. Pu and his men pursued him, cut off his head, and Zhou Ji of the Left Secretariat tracked down the remaining rebels and put them all to death.
